A Segment of Davide's Voyage Log

Day 16.
They all say that Rinascita's outer sea is riddled with dangers—storms, mist, reefs, and TDs that could swallow a ship whole. Some even claim that the world beyond Rinascita had already died in the Lament long ago, with only our isles left under Imperator's protection.
Pure rubbish.
They've let fear of the unknown take over. They think I'd never dare take a Gondola out to the open waters, saying I'm just a river rat full of big talk. Well, I'll prove I'm no coward like them!
Today I caught a fine fish. A good sign, I'd say, and a nice meal. Now I have the stars above to guide my way, what's to fear? Storms? Waves? Bring them on! As long as I have my Gondola, there is no place in Rinascita I can't reach.
Pilgrim's Sail

A nation of independent city-states scattered across a vast archipelago, with no central administrative center. Legends speak of Rinascita's founders, who fled their homeland and sailed to these islands to escape the Lament. 

As an island nation reborn from the Lament, Rinascita was long isolated from the rest of the world by relentless disasters and vast distances. It wasn't until recent times that the Rinascitans opened new maritime routes. Ships laden with their spices and minerals began to sail across the world, and in turn, new treasures and wealth began flowing back to Rinascita, enriching its shores.

Rinascita is famed for its unique "Common Echo" technology, which allows Echoes to persist in physical form within the radius of the Genesis Nexus. Through this technology, the Rinascitan people have integrated Echoes into every facet of their lives. This is how the nation came to be known as the "Land of Echoes."

Rinascitans place great value on the identity derived from bloodlines, and their society is built upon a deep reverence for family ties. For them, the welfare of the family always takes precedence over individual fate.

Ragunna City, the administrative center of the Ragunna city-state in Rinascita, is a thriving port city by the sea, its districts linked by winding waterways. The Ragunnesi are devout followers of the Sentinel, who believe Common Echoes to be gifts from the Sentinel carrying Their divine will.

In addition to their faith, the people of Ragunna are also known for their love of the arts. The city is adorned with magnificent sculptures and paintings at every turn, and impromptu performances often bring the streets to life. Under the leadership of Fenrico, the current Primus of the Order of the Deep, a series of laws have been enacted to restrict certain themes in artistic expression. These laws have sparked divided opinion among the city's inhabitants.

At present, Ragunna's daily affairs are overseen by the Order of the Deep, while prominent families such as Montelli and Fisalia also hold significant influence over the direction of the city.

The Carnevale is the grandest celebration of Ragunna, where the masquerades never end, wine flows like rivers, and music pulses through the night. During this time, people cast aside the weight of the world and surrender to the wild, unrestrained joy of the festival.

The Carnevale's origins trace back to Sentinel Imperator, who once guided the people of Rinascita. It began as a tribute to Their grace, a celebration where laughter and performance became the purest form of reverence.

At the peak of the Carnevale, the Sentinel is said to manifest and crown the finest performer with the "Laurel." This honor grants the bearer the privilege to commune with the Sentinel and hear Their wisdom.

Yet, a decade ago, the Carnevale was brought to ruin. A monstrous sea beast, rogue Echoes, and Tacet Discords swept through the festival, turning revelry to ruin. Only when Primus Fenrico intervened did the chaos subside. He proclaimed it was Sentinel Imperator's divine retribution for the Ragunnesi's indulgence and forsaking of their faith. Since then, the Carnevale has not been held again.

Those deemed faithless by the Order of the Deep are sent to voyage upon the Pilgrim's Sail, following the ancient path of those who once braved the mist and maelstrom seeking the Sentinel's guidance.

The Order claims that only Imperator can grant absolution to these transgressors. They must endure a grueling pilgrimage, suffering both body and soul until their repentance is complete. At the journey's end, it is said Sentinel Imperator will offer them forgiveness and the promise of new life.

But no one in Ragunna has ever heard of a faithless "pilgrim" returning from this sacred journey. The Order asserts that they reach Imperator's place of dwelling and devote themselves to Their service for eternity. While many still harbor doubts, few dare to openly challenge the Order—none wish to suffer the same tragic fate as those branded Fools.

A common boat-shaped Echo in Ragunna.

Ragunna's intricate network of waterways, coupled with its narrow streets and rugged terrain surrounding the city has made Gondolas the preferred choice for transporting both people and goods. For most Ragunnesi, they offer a peaceful, smooth alternative to the discomfort of navigating crowded streets or bumpy countryside roads.

Beneath their unassuming exterior, Gondolas are highly intelligent and deeply emotional. They communicate through distinct vocal frequencies, expressing their moods or responding to the command of their gondolier. Some, through specialized training, can even climb waterfalls.

The Order of the Deep worships Sentinel Imperator. In Ragunna tradition, the Order's clergy serve as the Sentinel's earthly envoys, entrusted with guiding the people in Their divine word.

The Order is led by the Primus, and the current Primus, Fenrico, has declared himself the "Enlightened One," the Resonator of the Sentinel. After the last Carnevale, he proclaimed to have discovered the way to commune directly with the Sentinel.

Beneath the Primus, the Priests oversee the rites and sacred duties of the Order, while the common clergy, known as Acolytes, spend their days poring over the Codex, spreading the Sentinel's teachings throughout Ragunna.

To uphold divine order, the Order commands three distinct branches:

Order Tribunal: The Order's secular judicial body that handles civil and criminal matters between families and commoners.

Chamber of Discipline: The Order's executive arm that commands the military to enforce the law. The Chamber heavily employs Echoes in combat, and its enforcers are often called "Inquisitors."

Order Penitentiary: The Order's religious court that trials heretics and faithless who question and defy the divine teachings of the Sentinel.

One of the most powerful families in Ragunna, renowned for their pioneering spirit. The Montelli family played an instrumental role in charting trade routes that not only connect Ragunna, but also greater Rinascita to the wider world. As the city opened its doors, the Montellis rose to prominence, amassing great wealth and unmatched influence.

The Montelli family also took the lead in introducing and developing Reserved Terminals across Ragunna. While the Order of the Deep dismissed these Terminals as an inferior mockery of the Genesis Nexus and Common Echoes, the Montellis secured the Order's approval to continue their development in secrecy, offering guarantees of safety and hefty tax payment in exchange.

Unlike the more traditional families, the Montelli family values emotional bonds and shared ideals above bloodlines and social standing. They advocate for the distribution of opportunities and wealth, believing that riches are worth more when they circulate. Though often ridiculed by traditional families as "nouveau riche with Shell Credits running through their veins," the Montellis take no offense—on the contrary, they wear the label with pride.

One of the most powerful, and certainly the oldest and most traditional, families in Ragunna, renowned for their expertise in medicine and poison. Their devotion to Sentinel Imperator is clear to all who know them.

A faction within the Fisalia family believes that the Montelli family's embrace of openness and the privatization of Echoes is a direct affront to Imperator's teachings, threatening to lead Ragunna into an abyss of heresy. They have directly opposed the Montellis through various means, shaking the family's longstanding image of dignified respectability. Yet, the head of the Fisalia family residing in Porto-Veno Castle seems disturbingly indifferent to the repercussions of these bold and provocative actions.

The Sentinel of Rinascita. In the faith of the Order of the Deep, They are often depicted as a being with the upper body of a horse and the lower body of a fish.

According to Ragunna's legends, Imperator guided its settlers to this promised land, offering them sanctuary from the threat of the Lament.

Though Imperator rarely reveals Their presence to the world, They maintain a connection with the people of Ragunna through the Laureate of the Carnevale, delivering divine guidance in the form of oracles.

In Rinascita, most Echoes can exist independently from Reserved Terminals within the radius of the Genesis Nexus. They are known as Common Echoes.

In Ragunna, the Order of the Deep governs the allocation and use of these Echoes. The people of Ragunna revere them as divine gifts, even as envoys of Sentinel Imperator. They treat them as friends and trusted allies, incorporating them into every aspect of daily life. This deep, symbiotic bond with Common Echoes is what has earned Rinascita its name as the "Land of Echoes."

Rinascita's central Resonance Nexus, also known as the Genesis Nexus. According to legend, Imperator revealed the secrets of the Genesis Nexus to the Rinascitans, enabling them to construct other such towering monuments that stand as symbols of the Sentinel's power and sovereignty.

Within the reach of the Genesis Nexus, Echoes can endure in physical form without relying on Terminals.

The Dark Tide is a Waveworn Phenomenon native to Rinascita. It manifests as a dark, swirling mass of clouds that gathers and eventually breaks, pouring down in torrents like a waterfall. Wherever the Dark Tide strikes, it spawns Tacet Discords, and the area around its point of origin becomes a new Tacet Field.

There have been two significant Dark Tides in Ragunna's history. The first, according to the Order of the Deep, was stopped by Napoli II, the first Primus of the Order. The second was quelled by the martyrdom of the Blessed Maiden Fleurdelys.

The Nimbus Sanctum is the only Sonoro Sphere that exists in the physical world, where mist and clouds are formed by concentrated Remnant Energy.

The sea of clouds that envelop the Sanctum is believed to be the lingering aftermath of the first Dark Tide. As the mist rose, it gradually submerged the former headquarters of the Order of the Deep, the Seminary of the Forgotten, forcing them to relocate to the Cathedral of Mercury in Ragunna City.

Local legends of Ragunna speak of a serene, mirror-like area at the heart of Nimbus Sanctum, said to purify the darkest of thoughts and transform them into part of the clouds. Many pilgrims, drawn by this tale, journey here in search of inner peace.

The Remnant Creature dwelling within Nimbus Sanctum. Legend holds that it was Lorelei's power that restrained the violent sea of clouds, sparing Ragunna from flooding.

Lorelei has the ability to cleanse the dark frequencies within the clouds, but she is not immune to their corrosive influence. As they accumulate to a breaking point, Lorelei will eventually become the Queen of the Night, unleashing her wrath upon all life that comes near.

A vault built by the Montelli family on the outskirts of the city. Within its walls lies the family's vast collection of treasures. The vault also provides public services such as secure storage for valuables, appraisals, and acquisition of rare collections.

The Fools who survived the dragon's assault—whom the Order refers to as the "pilgrims"—drifted on the warm currents, eventually finding refuge in a vast cavern on Penitent's End.

There, the Fools formed a troupe, determined to one day expose the truth hidden by the Order and return to their home. To achieve this, the troupe wrote numerous plays and "danced in chains," performing tirelessly across the archipelago.

For years, they have awaited the return of the Carnevale, hoping to expose the Order's secrets through their performance, claim the Laurel, and earn the chance to commune with the Sentinel.

[The Next Big Travel Hot Spot]: Egla Town!
For those brave enough to venture to the place that inspired the adventurous plays during the Carnevale, exploring the legendary realm of the mighty "giant," listening to the songs echoing from the sea of clouds by the water, or following in the footsteps of knights in pursuit of honor and justice will no longer be mere fantasies. In Egla Town, travelers can immerse themselves in breathtaking waterside scenery, observe the majestic migration of Tumbleyaks, and watch windmills spin gracefully on the plains, while bathing in the golden light of the setting sun. Alternatively, they can simply enjoy a peaceful afternoon tea and indulge in century-old delicacies, all while being surrounded by the vibrant colors of blooming flowers.

In this edition of [Dreamy Destinations], we journey to the mesmerizing Nimbus Sanctum hidden deep within Whisperwind Haven. A highlight of the enchanting Gondola cruise, the sea of clouds has long been a must-see destination, captivating visitors with its ethereal, dreamlike vistas.
Yet, few are aware that the Atrium of Reflections—often depicted in romantic tales—is not merely a creation of fiction, but the ruins of the highest spire of ancient Ragunna. To save its people, Napoli the Second invoked a miracle, turning the Dark Tide into the very sea of clouds that graces the land today.
The forgotten ruins of old Egla Town are now submerged beneath the sea of clouds.

[The Journey is the Destination] Embark Today!
It's worth noting that, although the reason remains unclear, the water level of Nimbus Sanctum has been steadily rising over the past decade, forcing the residents of Egla Town to move to the higher ground in the north.
Once, this area was a barren, undeveloped land, scattered with exposed boulders, and known as the Whisperwind Barrens.
However, the resourceful people of Egla Town began to build windmills that turned day and night, drawing water from the lower regions to nourish the land above. Their efforts transformed this rugged place into the thriving Whisperwind Haven we see today, where crops and flowers now flourish in the breeze.

(A short novel published ten years ago.
"An outrageous best-seller, banned by the Order three times!"
"Only one-tenth of readers truly understand it—are you one of them?"
"Incredible! The Russellian's satire remains as insightful as ever, even after all these years!"
So reads the editor's recommendation page… Clearly, this book stirred up quite a bit of controversy a decade ago.)

Far out across the stormy waters filled with jagged ridges and giant beasts on the surface of Solaris lies a group of small, unregarded islands. On this archipelago, the exiles-descended cultures are so amazing that they still think a unified thought is a pretty neat idea. These islands have—or rather had a problem, which was this: most of the people on them were unhappy for pretty much of the time.

After retirement, I kept thinking back to that afternoon when my friend and I first met.
Ford Percival. He was an alien.
On his first day in Egla Town, he ate ten baton bread without paying anything. Before the Divine Envoys could punish him for theft, I quickly paid off his debt.
Since the prayer, the Oracle of Mercy had wandered in my mind in search of something to connect with—until I met him, the poor outlander. He must have been starving.
"Hi, I'm Ford. I'm an alien. I'm analyzing your weapons. Quite odd components."
He said after I saved him. "And what is this place?" he continued.
An alien? Oh, I'd heard this kind of tale once from someone who claimed to be from a federation. He said Solaris was actually a living tomato—a tomato that could turn, breathe, even dance. And aliens, apparently, were from other tomatoes, living or dead.
"Egla Town," I replied.
"Egla Town, good. Wait, what is that?" He pointed at the windmills in the distance.
"Those are windmills. A cluster of Cyclop windmills, Briareos." Born and raised in Egla, I replied almost instinctively.
"C-Cyclops! Ah, I know about those! I've seen them before! But my stars—you actually managed to kill them? How did you people pull that off? Are those auto-rotating arrays made from their dead bodies? And what exactly is Briareos? A cooling device? A propeller engine? Or something to open up a network channel?"

(Continued)

After hearing my explanation, the self-proclaimed alien Ford seemed completely fascinated by the Cyclops. His emotions became so agitated that he plopped down on the ground, muttering some unintelligible words while pointing at the windmills in the distance.
So it was true—no matter where they came from, no matter what "tomatoes" they hailed from, anyone who laid eyes on the scenery of Egla couldn't help but fall in love with the chivalric literature.
So I straightened up, took three steps forward, and adjusted the nonexistent necktie, then explained graciously, "Exactly! That's right! Once, a righteous knight guided us to defeat the giant. Before that, all the people and Echoes in Egla Town were driven to the high ground in the south, fleeing from the giant's threat. Now, that oppressor lies buried beneath the sea of flowers. We built majestic windmills to irrigate the flowers and the farmlands, and named our past home Briareos, in honor of that knight's heroic deeds!"
After hearing my speech, Ford sat frozen on the ground, as if ten thousand Cetus the Tidebreakers had roared at him all at once, shattering his perception.
After a long pause, he asked me in disbelief, "Do you still have knights here?"
What did he just ask me?
Praise be to Imperator!
I could finally deliver the ranked No. 1 answer in the Top 10 Most Satisfying Moments for Egla People.
Putting on a solemn expression like the Acolytes of the Order, I envisioned a halo of nobility above my head, envisioned the almighty Imperator spreading wings before me, envisioned myself crowning a laurel at the Carnevale, envisioned standing in the grand church, wielding a sword as I was knighted, relishing the reverent gazes of the noble lords of Ragunna!
I replied, stressing each word with great emphasis:
"OF COURSE—"
"However, there are too many outsiders who seek the path of knighthood. Are you confident enough to accept the trial?"
The alien named Ford, whose Tacet Mark was blinking along excitedly, quickly grabbed my calf and shook it furiously, as if clinging to a log in the midst of a drowning. He cried out, "I am! I am! Please guide me to the legendary knight! As long as I can return to the planet Russel and save my hometown, I am willing to pay any price!"

(A feature on the culinary traditions of Ragunna.)

[Top Chef's Super Secrets]
Imagine yourself asking anyone on the streets of Ragunna, "Which restaurant is the best in Ragunna?"
Six out of ten will answer, "Trattoria Margherita!" Three will point to the family restaurant downtown, and the last one will say, "It's the place where the soft-tailed chef works!"
That's right! Such is the clout of Trattoria Margherita in Ragunna!
Amazing!
But what many don't know is that Trattoria Margherita is actually a family-run restaurant inspired by traditional Ragunna cuisine. From our investigation, we found that Egla Town still preserves this classic culinary tradition to this day. To maintain the special flavors of her dishes, Miss Margherita even takes time off to gather ingredients in Egla Town or Riccioli Islands!
Now, you might be wondering: "What? I can understand why Miss Margherita would go to Riccioli Islands for the fish harvest, but Egla Town? Isn't that a backwater town? And can the cuisine of Egla really be called Ragunna cuisine?"
Indeed, life in Egla isn't as thrilling as in the bustling Ragunna. People there live quietly, following the rhythm of nature. The town's trade and logistics are tied to Ragunna City. The people rise with the wind and rest by it, living a life shaped by windmills, wheat farms, and pastures.
But that's exactly why, for hundreds of years, the cuisine of Egla has remained unchanged. Here, the original flavors and cooking techniques of Ragunna have been preserved—using windmills to process crops and cooking food in traditional ways.
"This way, the ingredients and the food are especially precious! The cheese made from local pastures is creamy, and the meat is tender and flavorful! It's the perfect food to fill your belly!"
Miss Margherita commented during our interview.

[Comments from Special Guests]
Former Tax Envoy of the Order: The traditional cuisine is a remembrance of Rinascita's past. To forget it is to betray our heritage!
Orlando the Gourmet: The old man earlier sounded like he was chanting a slogan! What traditional cuisine? The bread from your town is as hard as a lethal weapon!

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part I)
...

At dawn, the Primus and I stood to bid farewell to the Pilgrim's Sail as it prepared to depart. Both the crowd and the acolytes watched with reverence as the believers boarded the ship. Only the most devout and courageous among them were chosen to embark on the Pilgrim's Sail, destined to meet the Sentinel in the distant sea.

For countless ages, Sentinel Imperator has rarely lingered in any one place, choosing instead to roam the seas, aiding vessels on their journeys. The Sentinel's guiding light has always led those lost upon the waves, helping them find their way back home or seek new lands for settlement. The Order believes that to face the storms and tides in search of the Sentinel's heavenly voice is one of the greatest honors a soul can aspire to.

Yet only those with practical experience can grasp the immense cost of each pilgrimage. Taxes and provisions are drawn from the commoners, skilled workers and sailors are taken from prominent families, and seasoned captains and chief mates are hired at great expense. All who embark on these treacherous seas are devout, but only those truly blessed by the Sentinel return with the promised glory and honor. Reflecting on history, the number of such fortunate souls is vanishingly small.

I have never questioned the purpose of the pilgrimage. My only concern is the immense cost it demands. Can we, in good conscience, allow these devoted believers to embark on a journey that burdens both mind and body? And as for our new Primus... What are his thoughts on this matter?

I looked to my side, surprised to find that my former seminary classmate, Lord Fenrico, had his face shrouded in a strange shadow.

...

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part II)
...

How has it come to this? After a sleepless night, I retreated to a secluded prayer room, seeking solace as I lay my confession before Sentinel Imperator. My hands trembled as I put these words to paper.

For a time, the Order ceased organizing large-scale pilgrimages, and the burdensome taxes were lifted. Though the people of Ragunna still honored the devotion of those who once sought the Sentinel across the distant seas, the Pilgrim's Sails had become a relic of the past. But everything changed after the bloody Carnevale... No, in truth, the shift began even earlier than that...

I still remember when the Primus delivered the order for correction, and I dutifully transcribed it: the Order would send violators of doctrine aboard the Pilgrim's Sails, stripping them of all official identities and setting them back onto the path of pilgrimage. Who could have foreseen that an act once meant to embody faith would come to serve as a form of punishment?

"The power of punishment and indoctrination shall be returned to the Sentinel," the Primus proclaimed to the assembled crowd. "Those transgressors who embark upon the pilgrimage in sincere repentance will, by their journey's end, be absolved of all transgressions and granted the Sentinel's forgiveness."

Yet no one truly knows if transgressors can fulfill their salvation, for no one has ever returned from the pilgrimage alive. "Those who commit acts of foolishness shall be sent to the Pilgrim's Sails"—this has become a steadfast law of the Order Penitentiary. Vandals defacing sacred statues, disloyal acolytes distorting doctrines, and even troupe members crafting satirical comedies—all have been condemned to the Pilgrim's Sails for their acts of blasphemy. Recently, however, familiar faces have joined their ranks, faces of those who had openly questioned the Primus's decrees.

I could have sworn my integrity on their faith and character, yet I stood by and watched as they were sent aboard the Pilgrim's Sails, doing nothing. No, it's no longer fitting to call them the Pilgrim's Sails. The common folk have given them a more appropriate name—the Fool's Sails, a vessel filled with those who have committed foolish acts.

Oh, Primus Fenrico... Is this the dream world you so passionately spoke of in the seminary?

...

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part III)
...

I was surprised at how calm I felt upon hearing the sentence from the Order Penitentiary. Perhaps my heart had grown as still as that of a dead person.

At dawn, like others before me, I was escorted by the Executors to board a Fool's Sail. Before the ship set sail, I glanced back at the port, only to find the Primus absent. Just as I expected, that man, now in control of unmatched power within the Order, has no need to concern himself with a fool stripped of his identity.

The Fool's Sails are nothing like the Pilgrim's Sails of old. Gone are the smooth, spacious decks and well-maintained sails. Instead, all I saw were rickety planks, loose screws, and splintered masts. The narrow cabins clearly lacked food and fresh water. I stared blankly at the other pilgrims around me. For now, we still manage to maintain some semblance of decorum and restraint, but I know that, before long, this ship will become nothing more than a cage filled with rampaging desires.

And even if we do reach the so-called destination, what awaits us there?

I once read the investigation reports sent back by the expatriate acolytes. That Penitent's End, shrouded in mist, is littered with the wrecks of Pilgrim's Sails. During those fateful voyages, the Fools who braved the storms never met the Sentinel. Instead, driven by the sea's undercurrents, they were cast ashore on that island, where the eerie glow of phosphorescence mingles with an unmistakable aura of death. I've even heard whispers of something far more terrifying lurking there, and the "Fire of Judgment"—a force so dreadful that even the Privy Council dares not speak of it.

...

Food is running out... Last night, someone lost control again, trying to lock themselves in the cabin to hoard the dwindling supplies...

O great Imperator, if you can hear my prayer, please grant us your final mercy through a storm. Absolve us from our misery, and let us... find peace at last.

(The remainder of the notes has been blurred by the seawater and is unreadable.)

A Transgressor's Transcript (Part I) In the ancient era, long before Ragunna was founded, the distant seas of Rinascita were the Realm of A Thousand Islands. At that time, the Fisalia family was already well-versed in the ways of the ocean. We extracted toxins and medicines from deep-sea plants, harnessed vast underwater resources, and reveled in great fortune and widespread renown. Later, with the assault of the Lament, the civilization of the archipelago teetered on the brink of destruction and our family became one of the founders of the Ark, embarking on a quest to find a new settlement. The journey across the sea was treacherous. The fleets of the Ark were either swallowed by thick fog or torn apart by fierce storms. Yet, our family's Ark, guided by a heavenly voice, led the fleet to a lush archipelago, following the faint glow of a distant lighthouse. One of those islands would later become what is now Ragunna. The newly founded Ragunna was still in a state of flux. To strengthen the family's rule, our family head declared that the manifestation of ▇▇▇▇ was a symbol of the deep-sea faith and a response from the marine divinity to our devotion. This proclamation proved to be successful. As the number of believers grew, so too did the stability of our family's power. Later, some fishermen claimed that they had been assisted by ▇▇▇▇ during their fishing trips. This entity, long known as the Giant One, had existed for ages. Its shadow beneath the sea guided Ragunna's fishermen and fleets, helping them weather storms and bringing in harvests far greater than before. The Fisalia family was the original ruler of Ragunna, and we also laid the faith foundation of the Order. Yet, why have generations of family heads chosen to conceal this history? Why can't I remember Its name? Cursed be it, the wound... it is throbbing again. Something must be wrong with the air... I must find a safer place. The soldiers will never think to search for me in the tower. I must document this secret history... before it slips from my mind entirely... A Transgressor's Transcript (Part II) The fishermen referred to the shadow in the sea as ▇▇▇▇, and they would call upon its sacred name to receive its aid. Small miracles began to accumulate, forming a powerful current of faith. The common folk grew increasingly convinced that the Giant One was, indeed, ▇▇▇▇. As the family began to investigate, they were shocked to discover that these miraculous occurrences differed greatly from those recorded in the past. So, what was the true form of the Giant One the people had placed their faith in? And what, exactly, was the true object of our devotion? This mysterious faith was quietly reshaping the history of Ragunna, and it even threatened our family's control over the Order of the Deep. Only the Ark forebears and our family heads knew that ▇▇▇▇ should be the true form of ▇▇. Yet, with the preaching of the Order, the common folk, unaware of the truth, began to place their faith even more in ▇▇▇▇. Meanwhile, rumors spread that the true form of ▇▇▇▇ was that of a fish-like deity. What's even stranger was that those who heard these rumors began to dream of ▇▇▇▇ in the form of ▇▇. Is this text truly the same record I once read in the secret chamber of the family head? I have an unsettling feeling that my hands are writing down the history about ▇▇▇▇ on their own. Ah, I remember now... Yes, even I, who have never set sail on the sea, was drawn into that dream as I fled. Beneath the tranquil surface of the sea, a giant dark shadow loomed, and my fishing boat felt like a mere sampan before it... Impossible... That impure, blasphemous form could not have been the object of my faith all this time. I must reveal the truth to the world. A Transgressor's Transcript (Part III) After the death of Napoli the Second, the Order of the Deep elected a new Primus. The spread of the faith surpassed all previous reach. Yet, the doctrines proclaimed by the Acolytes were tainted by a dark mist. Everything related to ▇▇▇▇ began to twist—its statues, its anecdotes, and even its proverbs... No one has ever suspected this mass hallucination. No one has ever resisted the dissipation of the form, for "every drop of water will eventually return to the sea." And what is its true nature? The power of Resonance wielded by Resonators is known as a blessing from Sentinel Imperator. Devout followers of the Order are granted this blessing by adhering to its precepts, allowing them to channel the divine force through mortal bodies. Witchcraft, however, arises from vain desires—faithless souls, drawn by Leviathan, form a contract to practice forbidden arts. In doing so, they forsake the divine blessing bestowed upon them at birth and abandon their humanity, transforming into witches who seek to taint the mortal realm with profane power. The Divinity has shaped our world, and all that we hold dear flows from Their blessings. Yet witches, seduced by the Arch Enemy, pervert these divine creations into impure, disgraceful entities, crafting a false Resonance with them. The enemy's mark upon these witches is proof of their transgressions. With the aid of the Vessel of the Enemy, they can even transform into Tacet Discords, posing a grave threat to Imperator's faithful followers. Caution is essential, for anyone who craves freedom and worldly desires is vulnerable to becoming pawns of Leviathan. Thus, we must regularly cleanse and exorcise such souls. If we allow these heretics to grow unchecked, wielding their tainted power to defile the mortal realm, they will inevitably bring the Dark Tide upon Rinascita. It is the Order's duty to guide and govern them, ensuring they align with Imperator's divine will. Should they refuse to join the Order, swear loyalty to Imperator's statute, or diligently uphold its teachings, their misguided fate will be set right by the Pilgrim's Sails. We shall pray for them day and night, that they may be saved by our Sentinel Imperator. Praise be to Imperator. The Spy Network of the Order the Deep Ah, my friend, my companion on this quest for freedom and truth, I implore you—open this pamphlet only in a secure place, away from prying eyes. What I am about to reveal is crucial to your safety. Learn now how to identify the spies of the Order the Deep and evade their grasp. All Echoes bearing a golden halo upon their heads are spies of the Order the Deep, serving as "Angels." They are always seen alongside the Acolytes, serving as the Order's minions to take out the heretics. Rinascita, the Land of Echoes? Ha... not even the greatest satire could ever truly capture the utter absurdity of the reality we endure. First, you must beware of those lantern Echoes, known as Lucerna. Though they may appear harmless, they possess the ability to reveal so-called heretics hiding in the shadows of the night. Their light can illuminate the path ahead, yet it also serves as a blinding weapon, causing one to lose their sense of direction. There was once an instance where someone used Fae Ignis's Echo ability to remain concealed, only to be exposed under the unforgiving glow of a Lucerna's light. Next, there are the most commonly seen plaster statues, the infamous La Guardia, the most loyal guardians of the Order. Without commands from the Acolytes, they stand motionless, like silent statues. However, if you find yourself pursued by La Guardia, do not waste time fighting them. Instead, focus on locating the Acolyte of the Order Penitentiary who is issuing the command. Among all these minions, the most detestable is Vox Sanctus, perched high atop the church buildings. They serve as the Order's guards of honor. While they cannot move freely, they use their instruments to preach false doctrines day and night. These sermons infiltrate the souls of the Ragunnesi, poisoning their thoughts. Can you imagine that the children of Ragunna are forced to hear this nonsensical preaching the moment they are born into this world? Oppression by force may still leave room for resistance, but in Ragunna, how can one escape the spiritual chains that seep into every corner of life? Laurel and Sword (Part I) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal, Volume 1 Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough The Golden Bough, a Ragunnesi narrative epic rich in history and deeply influenced by primitive religious culture, is renowned for its prominent theatrical elements. The epic begins with pastoral plays that draw on the primitive beliefs and customs of various tribes during the Age of a Thousand Islands. As the story unfolds, these diverse narratives converge under the guidance of Sentinel Imperator. The author employs the perspectives of the Divine Envoys to provide Imperator's view, allowing the characters to assume their roles in classical plays. Throughout the work, recurring symbols of religion and totems appear, echoing metaphors commonly found in traditional plays. The use of these theatrical elements has helped establish the epic as a beloved classic, cherished by both officials and commoners in Ragunna. Furthermore, it embeds the author's profound reflections on the will behind the Oracle delivered by Sentinel Imperator, as well as the social changes occurring in the region of Rinascita. ...(Some of the pages are missing) One of the most commendable scenes in The Golden Bough is the concluding Scene 3, where five storylines dramatically converge at the climax of the Carnevale: the Holy Forest of the Fagaceae Peninsula, the Order of Ragunna, the Keepers of Secrets in Thessaleo Fells, the successor of the governor in Septimont, and the gladiators, all merging in a grand finale. In this scene, the author masterfully interweaves characters and plotlines, capturing the unique allure of a grand historical tragicomedy. This convergence in Scene 3 has served as a template, inspiring countless plays thereafter. The scene's influence owes much to its intricate plot design, which displays a skillful technique that sets a standard in narrative structure. Beyond the theoretical framework of the work itself, this design—where each element reflects the core theme and draws from historical settings—has solidified this epic as a timeless classic, maintaining its relevance and reverence across cultural shifts in literary history. (See Note 23) The Golden Bough is recognized as the earliest work of art to connect tribal folklore with the Sentinel (see Note 24). In the climactic Scene 3 of the Carnevale, the five masks stand together, each pursuing their own faith, when Sentinel Imperator descends from above, bestowing the laurel upon the chosen Enlightened One—the main protagonist on stage. This ritual has since become a lasting cultural emblem in the hearts of the people of Rinascita. From this scene onward, every heroic journey must conclude with the ritual of "being laureated," whether the hero takes on the role of an actor on stage or a playwright behind the scenes during the Carnevale. Laurel and Sword (Part II) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough (Continued) The reason for Sentinel Imperator's descent at the climax of the Carnevale in The Golden Bough remains an open question, one largely unexamined in the epic itself or in related research. Historically, the prevailing view in the Seminary held that the Laureate must be the individual who most aligns with Rinascita's ideals and resonates with the Sentinel—not driven by dramatic passion or ulterior motives. For a long time, this perspective dominated studies of The Golden Bough and the broader field of Laureate literature, with the laurel seen as a symbol of immense honor and the embodiment of Rinascita's collective will. (See Note 25) However, following the cultural events after the Seminary incident, the Laureate's symbol and performances are now seen as expressions of the Sentinel's divine will—the guiding force behind delivering the Oracle and unifying the doctrines. The image of laurel has also come to represent this sacred intent. The author raises an intriguing question: given this interpretation, could the selection of the Laureate itself be seen as an indoctrination of freedom—a concept seemingly at odds with The Golden Bough? Can freedom, once indoctrinated, still be considered freedom? ...(Some of the pages are missing) [23] Charlie Welbeck, "The History of Reforms on the Rinascita Drama Aesthetics," published by Avinoleum Theological Seminary Culture Journal. Logbook_Number_#17
Mom, I miss you.
It's pretty misty here, and whenever it's like this, I can't help but think back to when I was little, back when we were together.
We used to live in a house out in the countryside. It was a thatched cottage, and in the summer, I could hear the dried hay on the roof crackling as the sun beat down. In the winter, the walls would get damp.
Inside, the house had a narrow hallway that led to the kitchen, where a broken lightbulb, somehow always mysteriously fixed, hung from the ceiling. The exposed wires were wrapped in black tape.
Along the hallway were two rooms. I slept in the smaller one, the one on the north side. The gauzy curtains, printed with the sacred verses of the Order, always felt a little eerie at night. When I couldn't sleep, I'd sneak out to the narrow hallway. It didn't matter if I kept my eyes open or closed. With my back against the damp walls, it was pitch black, and I couldn't even see my own breath.
The wind tried to sneak in through the cracks, and the door frame seemed to shrink. The old wires were starting to tear, and the damp air pressed against the bricks. My hair brushed against the wall, and behind it, a patch of quilt slowly shifted. All these sounds tangled together in my head, floating from my ears to my skin, then rushing back inside, shaking my bones with a soft, mesmerizing tremor.
I can't shake this feeling of dampness that echoes in my mind. Today, it's here again.
I just passed through the misty barrier on our route. It felt like an unsettling dream.
But don't worry about me. The safety manual says this mist can cause hallucinations, but it's harmless. I've made it through safely. Now, I need to check the inventory again, just in case someone took something while I was dreaming.
I really miss you, Mom. Don't forget what I promised. Once I've made my name here, I'll bring you to Ragunna.

... very few people, including those within the Montelli family know when the Vitreum Dancers first appeared, even though these unobtrusive, unremarkable Echoes have long served the family. In fact, most of the Montellis do not know of Vitreum Dancers as anything other than their domestic security detail. Thus it remains easily overlooked that no two Vitreum Dancers are alike.

Knowledge gleaned from the stained-glass artwork found in the ruins around Ragunna suggests that Vitreum Dancers were once Tacet Discord frequencies. They appear in stained-glass art along with general depictions of The Order's religion. To this day Montelli explorers have yet to find two identical panes of stained glass. The Order's artists took pains to alter the composition of panes that depict the same story or motif. This suggests that the frequencies of modern Vitreum Dancers each contain unique information, much like their Tacet Discord forbearers.

According to the book "The Wealth and Legend of the Montellis," the origin of the Vitreum Dancer dates back in history to a time when a Montelli ancestor received the Laurel during the Carnevale from Imperator who then instructed him to go to a tower abandoned by The Order. Upon his return, he would not divulge what he saw and forbade all Montellis from approaching the tower again. Undoubtedly this Montelli ancestor brought back the very first Vitreum Dancer. On his deathbed, his last words were that the Sentinel's Oracle would not exert influence over Montellis at present, but would determine their future course of events.

And with that the tower was barred to all subsequent Montelli, and as the family's cohort of Vitreum Dancers expanded, the legend of their origins faded into obscurity.
A Lost Page from a Diary

I saw it. There is no doubt. That long horn, dripping with the pitch-black blood of the sea. It has to be it. The boat we launched was capsized, its aft mast broken, and seven spears were lost. Many people were frightened and urged me to turn back... No, I will not stop. Of the seven spears, four were shaken off, but the other three lodged in its body. I saw them in its back, and the shattered crystals fell into the sea. This is day fifty-five. We are not chasing it; rather, it is standing in our way. Don't you understand? Only by killing it can we leave this room and reach the end of the infinite sea, to the place promised to us by the sails. Think! We have conquered every sea! From the Tacetite-eating Wyrm of the New Federation to the memory-devouring Dreadcurl Cuttle of the Forgotten Sea... How many of these things have I killed? Have we killed? Now this thing is in front of us! Every dream and thought that crosses your mind should be how to kill it! Give me that pipe, you old smokestack. I've walked through the haze with you all...I tell you, it took one of my legs, and I'll take it back from its heart! I have already seen the day it dies. Its blood will burn away in the sea, its flapping fins will droop, it will flip over, and finally, patches of milky white and deep red will finally appear... Then, everything I promised you will come true. You will have everything that is mine, be it money, oil, or faith—though I have no faith in any gods. You can take it all, even this ship. We will kill it. We must kill it. This is my fate, your fate, and this ship's fate. Now, I will extinguish your fire, whether it is the fear in your heart or the smoke in your pipe.

Impossible. Blessed by "Divinity"? I refuse to believe it. It is we who conquer the sea, not it! When storms tear the mast apart, and rocks smash the keel, where is Divinity's voice then? When we haul ropes and tighten sails, where is Divinity's guidance? We conquer it. It does not bless us! No, I will never yield. No god, no matter which one, can ever fulfill my revenge, our revenge and fate! Do not be cowered, do not be deceived! What others promise us means nothing. Only what we seize from the merciless sea matters! Prayers and blessings will not calm these waters, it is we who are the masters of this sea! Never stop! Even if it summons the entire ocean to fight against us, we must still complete our conquest! We must prove, beyond a doubt, that we are the true masters of this sea! Hoist the sails, ready the spears, and tighten the winches, lads! To the whirlpool! This tempest is the great wave pushing us forward, and this fierce wind only feeds our flames! Do not stop! Sail into the storm! Even if it means we must dive into the dark whirlpool and the abyss!

A Sealed Confession: Part 1

The person who escapes from the lacquered black abyss need not deliver any warnings.
 
It seemed to mock us as it danced within the swirling whirlpool. The blue crystals on its back gleamed, barely a few centimeters above the dark, rushing waters. The harpoons we had sunk into its back were gone, but we did leave three glaring holes behind!
 
Every time we neared it, it swam faster into deeper waters. The deeper it sank into the whirlpool, the faster it swam, but for us, there was no turning back.
 
It vanished first, and when it reappeared beside our port, one mast was already submerged, and the other snapped off.  

Then came the tightening of the winch and the splintering of the keel.

After that, there was nothing but darkness. In that void, I couldn't see my ship, my crew, or it.
 
At first, my "leg" twitched uncontrollably... I thought I had died.
 
I lay on the beach, alone. There was no ship, no crew, and no sign of it.
 
I had none of its blood on my hands, no ship's wheel, no ropes, no harpoons. Nothing to grasp onto. 

But the sea breeze felt unfamiliar. I realized I'd never set foot on this beach before. Since we set sail from Cape Bedford, I remembered every passing port and beach, but this one... this one was unfamiliar.
 
It wasn't until a young man, dressed in foreign attire, kicked my boot to check if I was still alive that I realized I hadn't gone to hell, nor had I ascended to heaven.
 
"Ugh...Where am I?"

"Riccioli Island, Rinascita"

"Rinascita...."

"Did you suffer a shipwreck at sea?"

"My ship... My crew..."

"There's no one else nearby."

"If that's true... then in the end, I only am escaped alone..."
A Sealed Confession: Part 2

...Later, I came to realize that we were "blessed."
 
The people of Rinascita said that whale guided ships and sailors who perished at sea to the afterlife, like a ferryman of the underworld. I heard that the merchants of the Forgotten Sea could weigh memories and souls on their scales, exchanging them for an equal weight of gold.
 
But for some reason, we're all still alive. Or rather, we exist in a state between life and death.
 
Yes, in time, I found Starbuck and Queequeg on this island. They're still alive. "It," the whale they call "Cetus the Tidebreaker," was also still alive.
 
How can this be a "blessing"? This is nothing but a "curse!" I cannot accept this!
 
Once I've had my vengeance, death may take me. But if my vengeance fails, I cannot bear to remain in this world as a mere plaything for those I sought vengeance against! My fate is mine to decide, and only true death can end my conquest.
 
They don't understand. That whale, though it appears tame and gentle, is cunning and violent. It transforms death into an unjust eternity, making my vengeance just a footnote in its mockery of the sea… No, I will never accept this. I will never compromise!
A Sealed Confession: Part 3

All whales carry oil, and this oil can dissolve many things that water cannot. This is the conclusion we reached after crossing every sea.
 
It can dissolve things of every shape and nature into one, and there are even stories of people who fell into a whale's oil-filled brain and drowned, with no bones ever found. But I have never seen what oil this whale holds... Perhaps I never will.
 
More than twenty years have passed, and Pequod seems cursed. No matter what Queequeg tries, we cannot repair her. My crew, those "resurrected" sailors, have long since forgotten how to wield their harpoons. They no longer know how to fight the sea.
 
And it seems as though the whale is toying with me. Since that time, whether at sea or ashore, I have never laid eyes on it again. I do not wish to give up. I refuse to. As long as I can kill it, I will be freed from this curse-like "blessing" to find eternal rest.
 
But I... I am too old now. I can no longer lift a harpoon. I cannot fight that giant creature aboard one of these tiny "Gondolas."
 
Yes, my ideals, my beliefs, my fate, my vengeance—everything is gone. Everything has been swallowed by these foreign seas.
 
You are, of course, welcome to mock me. The rope of that harpoon, while I lived, bound me tightly to that whale. Even now, after death, I am still bound by it. In the past, I was unwilling to sever that rope. Now, I remain unwilling still...  But I can no longer drag it into the black depths of the sea.
 
Sometime later, a young man came to find me. He said his name was Ishmael, a sailor's apprentice, and he wanted to learn how to fish.
 
At that moment, I recalled that before Pequod's final voyage, there was a sailor named Ishmael at the Bedford dock. But he did not board my ship. He stayed at the port, and if he is still alive at sea, he would likely be as old as I am now. How ironic...

"Cultural Insights"

Literary works draw their vitality from two sources: The creator and the readers.

The creator gives it new life, while the readers help extend it through reading. Each time they share a piece of work or publish their thoughts and reviews, they breathe new life into it.

Some may find the term "life of a work" elusive, as it's too abstract and intangible.

However, a parallel can be easily drawn from human life. When discussing the concept of life, one essential topic is inevitably brought up—name. A name is a symbol of existence, one of the most important markers that separate individual lives. If one desires to feel the vitality of a work, the most direct approach would be to feel its name, the various names bestowed by creators and readers.

I once heard an eerie tale from a land in the east that spoke of a lady with skin as fair as snow who would stand in a snowstorm, cradling a wailing baby in her arms, begging the passersby to hold the baby for her. If some kindhearted individual agrees to that request, they'd soon find themselves unable to let go, bound to freeze to death.

Intriguing, isn't it? But, by this point, it's a fascinating tale that evokes many distinct images that cannot yet form the entirety of "life." 

But what if we give it a name? Like... "The Snow Woman." This name alone captures the entire narrative and defines its essence.

However, even with the name anchoring people's imaginations, the unusual nature of words means each person takes a narrative differently.

Hence... The life of a creative work is less controllable than human life.

So, if one day, people's understanding of a work is led astray, then words could turn into a devastating weapon.

What would we do then? Show anger? No, absolutely not! Anger is the cheapest outlet of dissent. As creators, all we can do is believe. Believe that our words can live in their most genuine form.
<alignright/>—Exclusive interview with the Golden Anthem

This city, fractured and folded in on itself, seems trapped in some kind of temporal loop. Time moves forward and backward within a fixed range. But oddly enough, the plants don't seem bound by each "reset." The moss shouldn't be able to grow between the gears... unless time isn't flowing normally here. It's eroding, rushing, and spawning things that shouldn't even exist in the first place. Still, I'm grateful for this strange, unreasonable growth. It made me realize this city isn't beyond saving. There is a way out. (The pen seems to pause, leaving a small blot of ink on the paper.) There's one thing I still can't let go of. That rift... In my blurred memory, it sealed shut almost as soon as I was pulled into the storm. But if I can't figure out what caused it, or how to stop it. There's no way to guarantee it won't open again. And if it does... someone else could get dragged in. However, time's against me.
Sumika's Notes - Entry 136

Day 136 – Abnormal Pressure (If this constant pressure in my ears counts as such) Among the supplies Chisa brought back today was a can of oranges, the label printed with a production date long past... but that hardly matters anymore. These so-called "foods" are really just compressed Remnant Energy. Chisa gave the can to me. She sat off to the side with a piece of spring steel she'd salvaged, slicing it into a curved blade using her Forte, turning it into a new weapon. Watching her, I suddenly recalled another day. She was sitting just like this, halfway through organizing supplies on the sofa, when she turned and asked me what my Forte really was. I showed her a small amber, the one containing a preserved memory of the first time we worked together at this home base: the lights were dim, she was repairing a weapon, and I was taking notes on anomalies in the city's time flow. It was a rare, peaceful night, as long as we could ignore the fact that we were still trapped in a city sealed off from the outside world. To hold out against the erratic occurrences of the Lament, I once tried to learn Chisa's practical skills, but I failed. Of course I did. Still, she taught me a few special ways to leave markings. I remember what she said back then: "Stop treating everything like a science experiment. Think of every piece of scrap metal as a blade that never misses—" (The pen pierced the page, leaving a blot of ink.) And I know she truly meant it. This city, drenched in Lament, is riddled with danger. And yet, she always throws herself forward to shield everyone else. She thinks I haven't noticed how much she's burning herself out... doesn't know her body's running at the edge of collapse. But I've done the calculations many times. I know exactly how long she has before she crosses the breaking point. The only good thing is that this Sonoro seems to have stalled time and her condition. But I can't let her stay like this forever. I want to take her back. Back to the Black Shores, to the people I trust. There has to be a solution waiting there. I'll bring her back. No matter the cost.
Sumika's Notes - Entry 159

Day 159 – Sunny (A rare clear day) Today, Chisa told me she found a new spot that could serve as a base—an old, spacious cafe. From the large terrace on the second floor, you can see a beautiful view of the city center. It's been a long time since I've seen her this excited. It feels like we're one step closer to breaking the loop. And in fact, we are making progress. (The handwriting sharpens slightly.) Based on my research over the past few days, I'm now fairly certain of this: the key to unraveling this endless Möbius loop lies at the heart of the city—Neon Tower. It is the center of the Lament. The origin. And most importantly, the point that lies closest to the outside world. If we can reach the top, perhaps we'll be able to contact the people back at the Black Shores. Perhaps that's the way out of this Sonoro. The moss has already crept past the gears of my watch and reached the surface. Still, I haven't replaced it. It reminds me of time... and that something can keep pushing through falsehoods until it reaches the truth. I'll head for the heart of Neon Tower tomorrow morning. If time here is clay, then I will mold it into a road, one that leads us home.
Sumika's Notes - Entry 160

(The handwriting is noticeably rushed.) It should be around noon. I've reached the third floor of Neon Tower. Rubble from the buildings is scattered and floating around like a shattered kaleidoscope. Some pieces have even stuck to my clothes. I must look like I'm covered in rainbow frosting. …But my body is getting colder. Turns out I was right. Either these "sugar crystals" or the entire city are slowly draining the body heat of anyone who doesn't belong here. I need to keep moving. I have to find the right path to the top, and fast.
Sumika's Notes - Entry 161

15:23. It's been five full hours since I entered the Tower. Nearly half of that time was wasted, because I took the wrong path forward. My watch is almost entirely covered by moss. It spread so quickly. There's no doubt now. Time inside the Tower flows differently from the outside… No, the entire city of Honami is out of sync. I passed through countless time fragments, saw my tenth birthday party cake, the balloons and flowers from my coming-of-age ceremony, and the lab coat I first wore when I joined the Black Shores. It was happiness. Surreal like a dream… But I couldn't let myself get lost in it. I took off my protective gloves and ran my fingers across the corroded surfaces, trying to touch the reality in front of me. Surprisingly, it felt warm, like the vein of some living creature. (The writing wavers here, as if the hand holding the pen had started to shake.) …Or maybe that warmth was a hallucination born out of being so cold. My mind is slipping, but I can't stop now. I knew from the start this would never be an easy path... But so what? Even the most dangerous equation still needs someone willing to solve it.
Sumika's Notes - Entry 162

(The handwriting is distorted, yet forceful, pressing deep into the page.) Endless fragments of time... I didn't expect to witness my entire life play out in this place. Honestly? It was a good life. The repeated crossings and the blurring of my senses have made it impossible to judge the passage of time. Even the hands on my watch have stopped at last, caught in the moss's hold. But that's okay. I achieved my goal. After countless trial and error, I've finally mapped out every correct path. I know I probably won't make it to the top though... It doesn't matter. Even if I don't live to see the end, it doesn't matter. All I ever wanted was to lay down a clear road, so those who come after can walk across my bones and reach the light. That's enough for me. In fact… (The next words are nearly illegible, the ink smudged by a trembling hand.) I feel content. I remember that night when I was eighteen. I'd just passed the Black Shores assessment. I stood overlooking the sea by the Haven of Sprouts, gazing up at the sky. Back then, I believed the truth was hidden beyond the stars. Now I'm curled up inside the steel maze of Neon Tower, watching the Lament tear space part. Watching fragments of my past, my whole life... I've never been this close to the truth. Across time, I reach out to my eighten-year-old self. Space collapses around me. My mind catches fire in the light. I feel myself unraveling, being stripped away, broken down, and engraved. Then I hear my eighteen-year-old voice saying: "So you really made it here."

Record of the Knighting Ceremony

Long ago, it was right at this solemn and sacred site of trial that the Blessed Maiden was bestowed Haultir, the Sword of Virtue. Now, in the same hallowed place, the Blessed Maiden raised the Sword of Virtue high, her gaze fixed upon the squire kneeling before her. The squire held his posture with perfect stillness, silent as a statue.
 
"Before our Master Imperator, do you vow to fight only for justice and righteousness, and to lend your hand to the weak?"
 
The squire could not speak. He answered with a slow, deliberate nod.
 
"Do you vow to remain steadfast in faith and oath, never to abandon the duties entrusted to you?"
 
Again, the squire nodded.
 
"Even should you find yourself in the most dire of trials? Even should you... face death itself?"
 
The squire uttered an indistinct sound. From the tone, it seemed to be an affirmation.
 
The flat of the Sword of Virtue lightly touched Cadanto's shoulders—once, twice, thrice.
 
"From this day forth, you are a true knight, Cadanto."
 
For many of the Acolytes witnessing the ceremony, this was the first time they had seen an <ano=Divine envoy>Echo</ano> rise to knighthood.

As the Sword of Virtue touched Cadanto's chestplate, the duel between the Blessed Maiden and her Echo came to an end.
 
Cadanto knelt humbly in defeat. The crowd, who had been holding their breath, erupted into thunderous applause. At that moment, an Acolyte led a young girl through the excited crowd. Dressed in commoner's clothes, the girl clutched a large bouquet of blooming Firecracker Jewelweeds. The bundle was almost taller than she was. 
 
A gift for the Blessed Maiden, I assumed. Ever since she began her studies in Avinoleum, devotees had begun to make long journeys just to catch a glimpse of the girl blessed by the Sentinel. But this girl merely nodded toward the Blessed Maiden before turning toward Cadanto.
 
To everyone's surprise, the girl presented the bouquet to him. "So this is what you've been doing in my absence…" The Blessed Maiden smiled warmly. "Cadanto, accept the flowers. You've earned them."
 
Still silent, the knight laid down his greatsword and carefully received the bouquet. The little girl immediately leaned forward and embraced him, pressing her face against his cold armor. As always, Cadanto wordlessly bore both her tearful thanks and joyful sobs.
 
Cadanto… as many have said, is the Blessed Maiden's loyal servant and shield. But he is also a blade that protects the people.

"Excuse me... I'd like to read this book. Do I need to register here?"
 
Accompanying the timid voice before me was a biography, its cover bearing the portrait of the Blessed Maiden. I looked up from the desk and saw a small girl with pale violet curls. There was a mole just beneath one of her eyes. Tiny and delicate. Her skin was so pale that it was nearly translucent like someone who hadn't seen sunlight in a very long time.
 
"You're free to read anything here. Just remember to put the books away when you're done," I said as gently as I could, worried the solemn atmosphere of the library might frighten her away.
 
She was clearly not an Avinoleum student, yet she began appearing regularly in the library in the days that followed. She wandered between the circular shelves, always quietly absorbed in whatever book she picked up. Sometimes she asked me to help her find specific texts. Some were dense theological books, while others were thick volumes on the ocean or pharmacology—not quite the usual interests for someone her age. We grew acquainted. I learned that she'd been brought to Avinoleum by her relatives. They had their own matters to attend to and left her to wander freely in this comparatively safe library.
 
Her departure was as sudden as her arrival. That afternoon, as if answering some unseen summons, she closed the book in her hands and slid it back onto the shelf. I remember it. It was a study of the traditions of the Blessed Maiden in Ragunna. In the slanting dusk light, a long shadow stretched across the floor. Her guardian, presumably.
 
"Thank you for looking after me these past few days." She stood in front of me, doing her best to smile. "Cantarella... I'm Cantarella Fisalia."
 
That surname explained a great many things. Her belated introduction. The sorrow hidden in her words. The flicker of bitterness as she looked toward the door. I rose and took her hand. At the very least, I didn't want her to feel alone on the walk back to the threshold.

Torn Pages of a Journal

That woman who calls herself Talos took all of our food and forced us to obey her commands. She said this was the way of the Black Alley of old, where strength determines power and wealth, and the weak have no place. This order existed ten, twenty years ago, and even long before that. Brandon and the others tried to challenge her, hoping to liberate us from her "rule," but they failed. That was the last anyone ever saw of them.

Oh, I've heard plenty of stories about the Black Alley, all right. The evil they committed. How they eventually received the judgment and punishment they had coming for them. All we wanted was a peaceful life in the Black Alley. We never wanted to be like them, wreaking havoc in the city. We just want to live our own lives here. The Black Alley is our home.

I have a plan in mind. If all goes well, then I can escape this miserable dump. I heard that a hero named the "Blazing Nightwalker" took out the previous gang. Maybe I can find her and ask her to save the Black Alley again.

You missed your shift again, Cole! I'm not waiting around for you like I did yesterday. I'm heading back to my shack, grabbing a few drinks, and getting some sleep. I've done my part of the shift. If Talos starts asking questions, don't expect me to take the fall.

I'm off. I'm sure you know how to disarm the traps. Just follow the directions of the drawings on the ground. When the Runner brings in the new recruits, don't forget to open the gates for them.

Talos sent me to the city on errands for the next couple of days, so you're in charge while I'm gone, rookie.
Don't sweat it. Just follow my instructions to the letter, and you won't screw this up.

We open for business after six in the evening. During the day, put those kids on cleaning duty and make sure the broken bottles and mess from the night before are taken care of. No one likes a messy establishment. The Black Alley doesn't get any sunlight, so keep an eye on your watch and don't miss opening time.

Once people start to come in, hit the green button twice. Start things off with a track to set the mood. And remember: don't serve beverages just yet. If someone decides to make a scene about it, have Vincent take them to the ring and settle it over fists. If Vincent can't handle it, call Talos.

After a twenty-minute warmup, hit the red button once and the green button twice. Repeat this every half hour. I've prepped some banger music that they'll love. This is when you have the boys bring out the drinks. Once the vibe picks up, that's when the booze starts selling.

Keep in mind, whenever you see Talos show up, hit the yellow button right away. That'll play her favorite rock song, "The Black Alley Devils."

That's about it. She's all yours, rookie!

This is my fifth day in the Black Alley. People here are always on edge like they're afraid of something. No one says a word about it, of course.

The Black Alley is an oddity to the Ragunnesi. Youngsters these days don't even know it exists, while the old consider it a forbidden territory. Imagine the uproar it would cause in Ragunna if I wrote about its secrets and published them!

I met a nice fellow—everyone calls him the Runner, although I'm not sure who's pulling his strings. Thanks to his help, I got access to the Black Alley and its many mysteries.

The first three days of my investigation came up empty. But I did get to know a young man named Brandon over a game of pool. Seems like he's spent his fair share of time here. To be honest, he's damn good at the game, a worthy opponent, as long as he isn't cheating. Last time we played, the coat I had hanging nearby suddenly started burning. Luckily, I put it out in time, but by the time I came back, he had "scored" three points while I was gone.

Brandon is really tight-lipped about the Black Alley and always seems preoccupied with something. Still, I believe he could be the breakthrough I need in my investigation. He's not as stubborn as the old timers, nor as much of a pain to talk to as those masks. I still can't figure out where they came from. Maybe I'll figure it out someday.

Speaking of which, I haven't seen Brandon for two days. Maybe he went to help the starving old folks. As I learned during my investigation, the people here scrape by with odd jobs, barely managing to get enough food. Brandon is always sharing his rations with them.

Wherever he's gone, he'll be back for more pool. All I need to do is wait for him.

Brandon's not the only one who's gone missing. People have been disappearing left and right. Good thing I learned how to quickly memorize people's faces in school, otherwise I could've easily overlooked this.

Did something happen to him? Or maybe... he left it there on purpose as some kind of guide? Or as a warning? Those masks are watching every move I make, I can't just make a break for it. Maybe Brandon knows a way out. I have to find him.

That day, I recognized a familiar figure by the shelves in the Titular Repository. As I'd done in my youth, I tapped his shoulder. Andrea turned, recognized me, and murmured, "Teacher." He looked just as I remembered from our last meeting, yet years had slipped by unnoticed. He had come all this way just to see me. We found a quiet corner to talk.
 
Andrea spoke of his time as a traveling Acolyte, carrying the Sentinel's blessings beyond Ragunna to Riccioli, Septimont, Lilyland... through lands rich and poor, faithful and faithless. His journey must have been arduous yet extraordinary. The new wrinkles and scars on his face told me he was no longer that headstrong young man driven only by passion. His faith and ideals had forged him into a weathered knight.
 
But then, he began to confess. Not about duty, but about his daughter. It was the confession of a father, burdened with guilt toward a daughter he had failed. That kind of regret shouldn't have belonged to an Acolyte, so I did not offer the Sentinel's absolution in Their stead. The same devotion still shimmered in his eyes, and I knew he would continue traveling. Still a devout Acolyte. Still an absent father.
 
So I told him I was writing this memoir. I want to record my experiences here in Avinoleum, and in this very library. Most of them are trivial, yet each is a vivid reflection of the era I live in. These forgotten corners of history deserve to be remembered. The Sentinel teaches us to illuminate the world for others, and it's also important not to forget to light the way for those closest to us.
 
<color=Highlight>Titular Repository Memoir - Part II</color>

"…
 
On an otherwise ordinary closing day, I was carrying a stack of old books across the platform outside the library when I was drawn, almost involuntarily, into a crowd of onlookers. A duel held every gaze. As the Sword of Virtue touched Cadanto's breastplate, the match between Blessed Maiden and Echo came to an end.
 
Cadanto knelt humbly in defeat. The crowd, who had been holding their breath, erupted into thunderous applause. At that moment, an Acolyte led a young girl through the excited crowd. Dressed in commoner's clothes, the girl clutched a large bouquet of blooming Firecracker Jewelweeds. The bundle was almost taller than she was.
 
A gift for the Blessed Maiden, I assumed. Ever since she began her studies in Avinoleum, devotees had begun to make long journeys just to catch a glimpse of the girl blessed by the Sentinel. But this girl merely nodded toward the Blessed Maiden before turning toward Cadanto. 
 
To everyone's surprise, the girl presented the bouquet to him. After some explanation from the Acolyte, we learned that Cadanto had recently saved a family from Tacet Discords near Avinoleum's outskirts. The towering Echo knight remained half-kneeling and silent. He didn't seem to understand why a human would offer him flowers, or perhaps he felt unworthy of such thanks?
 
"So this is what you've been doing in my absence…" The Blessed Maiden smiled warmly. "Cadanto, accept the flowers. You've earned them." 
 
Still silent, the knight laid down his greatsword and carefully received the bouquet. The little girl immediately leaned forward and embraced him, pressing her face against his cold armor. As always, Cadanto wordlessly bore both her tearful thanks and joyful sobs. 
 
Cadanto… as many have said, is the Blessed Maiden's loyal servant and shield. But he is also a blade that protects the people."
 
<color=Highlight>Titular Repository Memoir - Part III</color>

"…
 
Retirement drew closer with each passing day, and time flowed quietly within the library. I thought there would be no more ripples.
 
"Excuse me... I'd like to read this book. Do I need to register here?"
 
Accompanying the timid voice before me was a biography, its cover bearing the portrait of the Blessed Maiden. I looked up from the desk and saw a small girl with pale violet curls. There was a mole just beneath one of her eyes. Tiny and delicate. Her skin was so pale that it was nearly translucent like someone who hadn't seen sunlight in a very long time.
 
"You're free to read anything here. Just remember to put the books away when you're done," I said as gently as I could, worried the solemn atmosphere of the library might frighten her away.
 
She was clearly not an Avinoleum student, yet she began appearing regularly in the library in the days that followed. She wandered between the circular shelves, always quietly absorbed in whatever book she picked up. Sometimes she asked me to help her find specific texts. Some were dense theological books, while others were thick volumes on the ocean or pharmacology—not quite the usual interests for someone her age. We grew acquainted. I learned that she'd been brought to Avinoleum by her relatives. They had their own matters to attend to and left her to wander freely in this comparatively safe library.
 
Her departure was as sudden as her arrival. That afternoon, as if answering some unseen summons, she closed the book in her hands and slid it back onto the shelf. I remember it. It was a study of the traditions of the Blessed Maiden in Ragunna. In the slanting dusk light, a long shadow stretched across the floor. Her guardian, presumably.
 
"Thank you for looking after me these past few days." She stood in front of me, doing her best to smile. "Cantarella... I'm Cantarella Fisalia."
 
That surname explained a great many things. Her belated introduction. The sorrow hidden in her words. The flicker of bitterness as she looked toward the door. I rose and took her hand. At the very least, I didn't want her to feel alone on the walk back to the threshold."

Every Gladiator in Septimont knows this place. It's where we hunt and test our mettle.
