It's been forty-eight hours. I don't think they'll find us now.
 
You've done well, old friend. This is where your journey ends. I never expected a Sabercat Reaver. Without the proper tools, I can't fix you.
 
It seems I was born worthless and will die the same. I had originally hoped for you to record the effects of the Void Storm on the human body and the surrounding environment when I entered it, then deliver the data to the Spacetrek Collective. A coward's last shred of dignity.
 
The Academy will find the note in my room soon enough. Yes, this is a journey to die. I intend to let the Void Storm take my life.
 
Perhaps someone will find this journal long after I'm gone. Let it serve as my farewell to you, stranger.
 
Forgive me for leaving without a proper farewell. Please understand, this isn't a sudden impulse, but the final compromise after a long and painful struggle.
 
As a researcher who once held science as my faith, I believed that the pursuit of knowledge is civilization's most noble mission. My field once granted me glimpses of the universe's profound beauty. Those elegant equations on the blackboard seemed to guide me toward pushing open the doors of progress.

But perhaps every era is destined to face the same tragedy. Researchers believe they stand on the shoulders of giants, only to look down one day and find themselves standing on the ruins of their own idealism. Failure, after failure, after failure... Was this always my limit?
 
That's when a colleague reached out. He claimed he could help me overcome my technical bottlenecks, but everything had to be done in secret. I later discovered he was a Fractsidus spy. On the day he was captured, he never revealed our collaboration. He only left me with a smile. What was he smiling at? That I was next? Or that I was no longer the man I used to be? In our work together, I had already crossed lines that violate scientific ethics.
 
The purity of knowledge in my eyes had long been corrupted. Whenever I heard my colleagues' praise during academic conferences, I felt my stomach twist. Their admiration was evidence of my betrayal of science.
 
Death is all that's left for me now. But even though my soul is sullied, I wish to leave one last, small thing of value before I go.
 
The Void Storm. None would volunteer to enter it. I imagine if someone would go into it... It would certainly garner data of immense value.
 
I do not seek forgiveness, nor do I expect to be understood. I only hope my departure becomes a question mark, lingering in the minds of those who still believe in the purity of knowledge...

Death only gives one chance. I can't waste it. First, I must observe the Void Storm. Perhaps I'll stay with the Roya tribe until I'm ready.

Time has lost all meaning to me. It's nothing but a countdown now.
 
I haven't encountered the Void Storm yet, but I've learned much from the Royan archives. Their records speak of survivors. What allows one to live through it? Where is the line that decides what gets erased and what remains?
 
Ugh... this fever won't break. I should set aside these heavy thoughts for today.
 
Why is it that whenever I relax, I am reminded of the Roya tribe members from when I first arrived?

I watched them live alongside the Exoswarm, toiling with simple tools. I saw them observe the night sky and strange phenomena with their own eyes, patiently calculating, step by step, summarizing patterns.
 
At night, they would sit around the campfire. No one dwelled on the day's troubles. They simply planned for tomorrow, then sang a song with a strange, simple, repetitive melody, as if speaking to Lahai-Roi. Or perhaps it was their way of encouraging themselves.

Watching the firelight dance on their faces—wrinkled and young—a profound confusion struck me.
 
We, in our "advanced" civilization, seek to master nature through technology, to eliminate all uncertainty and pain. When progress stalls, we despair, even betray our morals for a breakthrough. We believe human dignity lies in "conquest."
 
But for the Roya... even though a "small" storm could wipe away everything they worked so hard to build, they show no despair. Their dignity isn't about "conquest." Instead, they chose silence. Time and time again, they bend their bodies, measure the broken land with their feet, and begin anew.
 
I once despised this "inefficient" struggle, seeing it as a sign of an unprogressive society. But now, what rises in my heart is… respect.
 
Such a feeling of contradiction claws at me from the inside. The "pure science" I've pursued my entire life, if it ultimately led me to betrayal and nihilism, then where is its purity? These tribal people, who knew nothing of "science" at first, have proven a more fundamental purity through their very existence—the will to struggle and live, no matter how many times they're beaten down.
 
Here I am, the lofty professor, brought down from my high horse. I'm driven to suicide by the "impurity" of my ideals, while they, with their hands in the dirt, fight to live. In that struggle, they embody life's truest purity.
 
The rain outside grows louder, much like their song… I'll leave once the fever breaks. I need to get closer to the Void Storm, to understand it more. My old droid friend may be broken, but I still have a way to record it all. If I remember correctly, there should be an Outcast camp up ahead.

This is likely my final recording. I haven't formally introduced myself yet. I am Sestan, a professor from Startorch Academy.
 
I don't know what awaits me now...
 
I was perched at a high point, recording data on the Void Storm. While adjusting my instruments, I saw a mech reindeer, unaware, drifting too close to the edge of the distortion. Slowly. So slowly. I knew an invisible force would snuff out its fragile life in an instant.

In that moment, my mind went blank.
 
I did not weigh the value of life, did not calculate the odds of success, did not look back on a lifetime of sins and confusion. My body acted before any rational thought could intervene.
 
I rushed forward and pushed the reindeer out. And I was pulled in instead.
 
Life is full of surprises. To be honest... I had already let go of any thought of suicide. This journey, the people I've met along the way... they showed me how.
 
In the Roya tribe, I witnessed the strength of the human spirit. In the Outcast camp, among fellow traitors, I learned about forgiveness from their struggle to survive. Everyone was just trying to live, while I was wallowing in self-pity, clinging to the guise of an idealist.
 
My life and my ideals had strayed from their path. And so... in this moment, I rushed forward. Not just toward death, but toward a reunion with the true spirit of science: to protect life, no matter how small.
 
Before I vanish completely, I'll try to remain conscious. I will record my physical sensations and the frequency fluctuations, then upload the data to this Cassette and a data drive. Consider this my final observation report. I hope it proves useful.
 
Body temperature: normal... Wrist movement: normal... Feet, hmm... losing sensation...
 
………………
 
Twenty-three minutes have passed...
 
…………
 
Hmm... Death, is it always this quiet? I used to think my students were too noisy. But now, haha, I find myself missing the noise...
 
External sound... decaying rapidly...
 
Hmm... after the sounds disappear, will the light go next...?
 
Finally... I'm home...

Evans

6. Do not perform safety-critical tasks while fatigued, in poor health, or under significant emotional distress.

1. Food and Beverages For your safety, eating and drinking are strictly prohibited while the Express is in motion. The risk is significantly higher during vertical transit phases within the Starward Riseway. The high acceleration forces present a severe health hazard if consumables are ingested. 2. Pets, Bionic Units, & Exoswarm To maintain onboard safety and order, all pets and bionic devices must be checked in for transport. Live animals must be placed in sturdy carriers. Bionic units must be powered down and stored in secure containers before check-in. Bringing them into passenger carriages is strictly prohibited. Exoswarm may board only in designated compartments under the supervision of a licensed Shepherd. Exoswarm must undergo prior training to prevent panic responses during sudden acceleration, which could compromise the safety of all onboard. Jumping During Vertical Acceleration or Descent This rule may sound absurd, but every absurd rule comes from an even more absurd real incident. They fabricated exoskeleton rigs, smuggled them aboard, and attempted to "challenge the laws of nature." Under the stars, we are both observers and part of the cosmos itself. When you close this guide, your real journey has only just begun.

Forget the names of the constellations. What matters is that you looked up and let the starlight in. The moment you first lost yourself in the beauty of the stars is more precious than any astronomical fact.

A gentle reminder for every stargazer:
1. There's no need to bring advanced telescopes. A curious heart is all you need.
2. Pick a night when the moon is shy, and the sky is clear.
3. Bring a star chart, a flashlight, and a friend who'd love to share the quiet of a starlit night with you.

When the starlight touches you, remember this: every cell, every fiber, every element that makes you you was born in the heart of a star. You are, in your own way, stardust made manifest.

May the stars always bring you peace and inspiration.

Dedicated to all those who have ever stopped and looked up.

She mixed me a drink once, called "Starfall."
It was the most exquisite taste I've ever known.
But she left no recipe.
She said it wasn't necessary. That even with a recipe, the taste could never be recreated.
"If you love it," she told me, "then cherish the moment you drink it."

She said eternity is a lie, a delusion.
"Then what is real?" I asked.
"The answer is where a river of stars falls. Come with me, and we'll see it together."
But I could not go.
Our visions of life were too far apart. I would not yield.
So I swore I would recreate the taste of "Starfall."
What was in it? Grenadine, Bols Blue, sparkling water, salt on the rim, and a lemon wedge.
Or was there something else?
Perhaps a hint of regret, or the weight of a sigh?

She always loves fleeting things.
She loves the flicker of light, the glow of dusk, the fall of a flower.
Meteors in the night sky, ripples on a lake.
She loves the tide rising and falling.
A dancer leaping in midair.
And most of all… fireworks.
Those moments are beautiful, I know.
But what comes after?
How do I face their vanishing?
I wish such moments could last forever.
But she never seemed to care.
I don't understand.
I truly don't.

Should you become stranded on ice after a slip or fall, do not attempt to stand up on your own, as concentrated ground force may cause the ice to fracture, or you may suffer injuries from falling a second time. Today, I walked through the valley of the shadow of death. I was surrounded by a swarm of Tacet Discords.
Right when I'd given up hope, I heard a noise. It wasn't the wind, but a crisp, rhythmic "ding... ding..." like a sharp blade tapping against ice.
I forced my eyes open. They were practically sealed shut with the frost.

▇ is not reactive in the conventional sense, but its alignment shifts under different lighting conditions.

I'm not going crazy. I'm not going crazy. I'm not going crazy.

[Wegener - Note 2]
We had an argument.
Daniel said he saw "▇▇" moving under the ice. Amundsen said it was just a shadow.

▇ has no face. So ▇ borrows them.

▇ isn't imitating us. Something is using us, trying to become "us."

Just a little closer.

Violence has occurred.

I saw Daniel walking toward me, but his shadow was in the wrong direction.

Just like the professor said, only I, only my Forte, can save that village from being wiped out. I couldn't save my own home back then. But this time, I won't stand by and watch the dark take the people I love.
It's time to go.

I never imagined old tech from my hometown all those years ago would find a new life in an expedition motorbike. Even now, the mention of the "Inferno Rider" still strikes fear into people's hearts. New Moon, where light finds its fresh start.
One of Septimont's divinatory Lunar Phases. The New Moon heralds the dawn of the lunar cycle, with its surface veiled entirely in shadow.
The New Moon symbolizes rebirth and a new beginning:
After its long journey through the heavens, the moon circles back to its starting point, renewed and ready to begin anew.

Crescent Moon, where light begins its spread.
One of Septimont's divinatory Lunar Phases. Following the New Moon, shadows start to retreat, and a sliver of light graces the sky.
The Crescent Moon symbolizes growth and hope:
The delicate arc of light grows fuller night by night in the eyes of those who gaze upward.

First Quarter, where a bow of light is drawn against the veil.
One of Septimont's divinatory Lunar Phases. It is a half-lit moon, bright on the right, where light and shadow evenly divide the lunar surface.
The First Quarter symbolizes action and challenge:
After a long wait, the time to step toward the full light has finally come.

Waxing Gibbous, where ascent awaits.
One of Septimont's divinatory Lunar Phases. It is the time when the Full Moon is near, shadows are almost gone, and moonlight brightens the night.
The Waxing Gibbous symbolizes adjustment and preparation:
The restless edge of transformation calls for self-adjustment that leads to a breakthrough.

Full Moon, where clarity rules.
One of Septimont's divinatory Lunar Phases. The moon reaches its brightest, wholly unshadowed and facing the world in full.
The Full Moon symbolizes wholeness and release:
The flawless silver mirror reflects the purest dreams held in every heart.

Waning Gibbous, where brightness dims yet lingers.
One of Septimont's divinatory Lunar Phases. After the Full Moon, darkness returns, and the light begins its quiet retreat.
The Waning Gibbous symbolizes reflection and sharing:
All things wax and wane, so joy and sorrow are intertwined by nature's design.

Last Quarter, where darkness reclaims its share.
One of Septimont's divinatory Lunar Phases. It is a half-lit moon, bright on the left, where light and shadow evenly divide the lunar surface.
The Last Quarter symbolizes release and decision:
In the shifting tides, seasoned sailors know when to let go.

Waning Crescent, where only a glimmer remains.
One of Septimont's divinatory Lunar Phases. The final stage of the cycle, with only a faint shimmer clinging to the edge of shadow.
The Waning Crescent symbolizes rest and settlement:
Even the grandest journey calls for a pause to gather breath.

Twin Moons, where two lives intertwine. 
A unique and unpredictable Lunar Phase in Septimont. Two crescent moons rise back to back in silent symmetry.
The Twin Moons symbolize trust and friendship:
With a steadfast ally by your side, even the longest night loses its terror.

Rippled Moon, where changes return to one.
A unique and unpredictable Lunar Phase in Septimont. The Rippled Moon shimmers with layered, wave-like brilliance that flows across its surface.
The Rippled Moon symbolizes eternity and flux:
In this world, only the whirl of ceaseless change endures forever.
During the current phase, each level increases ATK and Max HP by 3.2% and DEF by 0.25%.

The Pioneer Association, originally known as the Universal Geography Association, is a scientific and educational organization established before the Lament.

After the Ebb Tide, the Association collaborated with scientists, photographers, and journalists to continue exploring the mysterious world after the disaster, and shared the discoveries with the public through magazines, maps, books, on-site entertainment experience projects, and interactive media, attracting a large fan base in the six regions.

Lollo Logistics is a widely respected global transportation company, known for successfully handling high-risk transportation assignments. Their philosophy of "harmony brings wealth" guides their team in choosing peaceful resolutions to any challenges they may face.

The Cruising Drake, a group of inventors and enthusiasts scattered throughout Huanglong, set up shop in the bustling Jiaolong Repair Shop. They are known for their love of gang culture and their ability to raise funds for their ventures. Their specialties include causing mischief and creating innovative inventions.

Exiles is the general term for groups of people who wander outside the city and live by crime and scavenging. The Exiles do not have a unified organizational structure, and the strongest person in each camp will act as the leader to give orders. In the Huanglong area, they are mainly concentrated in the Wuming Bay. Due to the large number of people and different ideas, two gangs have been formed. The "Boar Gang", for some reasons, seems to be not so repulsive to outsiders.

A clandestine organization with an extreme obsession with power and progress that borders on macabre. The Fractsidus members are rumored to possess an unusual appearance, but further details are still being uncovered through ongoing investigations.

The Black Shores are a mysterious organization dedicated to saving the world from destruction. They travel to the most perilous places, recruiting brave allies and never losing their idealistic passion. Those who join or are invited to their island will don the emblem of a Blake Bloom as a symbol of their membership.

This flower is for you. I hope it makes you happy!
Hee-hee. Hi, there! I'm Encore from the Black Shores! Wanna go on an adventure with me and my Woolies?
Calcharo, leader of the Ghost Hounds Mercenary Group. I suppose you've heard about what we do. Don't worry, your safety as my client will be guaranteed until the job is done.
I am Jianxin, the successor of Fengyiquan. Thank you for your hospitality. Would you mind sparring with me?
You're probably more used to seeing me as that liondancer on the high poles, I guess? Let's hang out more! I want you to remember me as how I look, without the lion head!
Jiyan, of the Midnight Rangers. Protecting our lands and people is my solemn duty. Should you encounter any difficulties here, I will do my utmost to help.
Name's Yinlin. As for what I do... Shhh, we don't talk about that in public.
As the Sentinel said, we will meet here.
It is truly my fortune to find a worthy opponent like you in this vast world...
I'm Zhezhi… I do commissioned paintings. Um, what else...? Oh, I'm open for commissions! I offer fair prices, can adapt to any style you need, and do revisions too. And I never miss a deadline!

My name is Xiangli Yao, a researcher at the Huaxu Academy. Rover, your rare resonance frequencies raise an intriguing question: are you a unique beacon of insight in our quest for truth? Or do you already hold the ultimate truth in your hand?
"The Shorekeeper"... This name suits me well enough. It aligns with my purpose and drive: they only exist because of you.
Camellya, a Bloom Bearer of the Black Shores. Happy to see you again! My beloved... seed of fate.
Fate has led you to me, and considering the terms I'm offering… You wouldn't refuse me, would you?
All the world's a stage, and we are mere players.
I'm Phoebe, an acolyte of the Order. Praise the Sentinel. May They guide you to compassion and enlightenment.
Brant's the name, captain of the Fool's Troupe! A pleasure to meet you. Enough with introductions now—let's hand the stage over to everlasting joy and boundless liberty!

The current head of Fisalia, Cantarella, the Bane. Whether I am the Bane of the wicked or the pure is yours to decide. Shh, no need to answer. The moment you arrived, the ripples that surrounded you told me all I needed to know.

I am Ciaccona, a wandering bard from Rinascita. Should you harbor any unspoken thoughts or deep emotions, why not convey them into poetry? When you pour your heart into words and music, you speak directly to people's hearts.
Name's Zani, Averardo Vault employee. You're my client, huh? If so, I'm your sword and shield. Just say the word. If you leave me a good review when we're done, it'll be much appreciated.

Cartethyia, now a wandering knight. The Threnodian's malicious creation, the Order's unsuspecting Laureate, the defier lost in the tides of fate... These titles, once portrayed in poems and books, have long since slipped from my grasp. As for what lies ahead... let's explore it together, "Swordbearer."
Lupa, Gladiator of Septimont. Just ignore the attention, Warrior. This victory is ours to savor!

Do not fear the Fractsidus Overseer. Settle your mind. Quiet the clamor of thought. Only then can you stay and truly appreciate the perfect melody echoing through the Lycoris sea... and the true paradise that is soon to arrive.

I am Augusta, Ephor of Septimont. Etch this name into your memory—it belongs to the one who stands above, and whose mark will never fade. Whether we meet as foes or friends, my sword and I await the fierce fight between us.
Beyond myself. Beyond every written start and end of the story. Till we rewrite our fate.
Galbrena. The Fiend of Ever-burning Flame. The Discord Slayer. Call me what you want. Just point me to the monsters.
Qiuyuan, a blade drawn at your word. Wield me as you will.
Kuchiba Chisa. Tactical Development Program, Department of Engineering, Startorch Academy. Forte Specialization: structural dissection... Apologies, this might not be the time for formalities.
Outlaw Blue, Apollo Orange, Hazard Yellow, Acid Green... Wanna guess what color is my next pick?
I am Mornye, Research Institute engineer and professor at Startorch Academy. Please, let me know when my expertise can be of service.
Aemeath, Synchronist of the Exostrider from Rabelle College. That was me back when I was alive. Now? I'm a digital ghost!
Dr. Luuk Herssen, from the Resonator Nursing Unit. A rare exception that we meet outside my office. Oh, you can just call me Luuk.

Deep scratches on the wall. Flimsy debris. Weapon fragments that cannot be ignored… The prototype patrol mech proves far more dangerous than anticipated.
Seeing a reflection of her own past in the crisis, Lynae chooses to focus on locating the rogue mech and gives the student a chance to confront his own fears. All signs suggest the trail leads beyond the Celebration site.

The truth behind the dangerous rogue mech finally surfaces. Its aggression was born of a desperate desire to protect. After losing his family, the student built the mech as a fragile yet desperate shield. But just as the dust begins to settle, the disabled mech suddenly jolts to life and bolts toward an unknown destination.
Turns out it's a move to save its creator from the contaminated Exoswarm. With the chaos behind you and everyone safe, you and Lynae return to the Academy, letting out a long-overdue sigh of relief.

The student received a just punishment for his actions, but also the support his talent deserved. Life at the Academy continues on, unchanged. For Lynae, however, the incident has sparked a question about her own path forward within. Enjoying the campus life here is no longer just a fragile dream. It's her everyday reality now. Under the vast blue sky, she cracks open a soda and begins to share her new wishes with you...

To match the warmth and wonder of the New Solar Celebration, Luuk Herssen has baked a fresh batch of waffles. A message arrives at your Terminal riding a beam of sunlight—an invitation as soft as a waffle and as rich as a latte.
It's such a sunny day. While you have a moment, head to the infirmary to try Luuk Herssen's latest creation.

Luuk Herssen has put a new tweak on his recipe, and you're the first to get a taste. The infirmary is rarely this quiet. Usually, the endless stream of injured or sick students during the Celebration keeps the staff running off their feet.
While you and Luuk Herssen exchange recent campus anecdotes, an emergency at the venue cuts your peaceful tea time short. With a hurried "Until next time," your time together comes to an abrupt end.
Remember to take breaks when you can. A little afternoon tea goes a long way.

Based on your feedback, Luuk Herssen has refined his waffle recipe once more. Yet, the fresh batch vanished mysteriously just two minutes after he left! What kind of being could act so fast? To recover the stolen treats, Luuk Herssen has sent you a "commission." 
Head to the infirmary and begin your investigation into this Case of the Missing Waffles.

The infirmary is a revolving door of people, and the clues are a tangled mess. But within the detective game Luuk Herssen has so meticulously crafted, you peel back the layers of the mystery and lock onto the prime suspect: the calico cat that frequents the infirmary.
When you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth. Now, it's time to hunt down the suspect...

In the final stage of your detective game, you have deduced the identity of the thief who made off with the waffles in under two minutes, but the important waffles remain gone. Where would a tiny feline suspect hide its spoils? 
"A place not far from here, quiet, undisturbed."
Following this lead, head to the preparation team's warehouse with Luuk Herssen.

Among the piles of clutter in the warehouse, you find the suspect and the "remains" of the waffles. With the cat safely in custody, you and Luuk Herssen weigh your next move.
You lay out your final theory. The tea time in the middle of a busy day and the impromptu detective game were Luuk Herssen's way of helping you unwind. Your "assistant" surrenders at your sharp deduction, admitting his ruse and promising to go out and truly enjoy the celebration with you.

The suspect cat has been apprehended. Detective, it's time for the wrap-up.

Luuk Herssen messages you that while he was relaxing at the celebration and scouting for potential adopters, the kitten got spooked and slipped out of its cage. 
A "criminal" like this cannot be allowed to roam free! For the safety of waffles everywhere, head to the teaching building, track down this fluffy fugitive, and bring it back to the infirmary.

After bringing the calico back to the infirmary, you and Luuk Herssen discuss the kitten's future. You suggest that he adopt the cat himself, an idea he readily accepts.
Welcoming a new life into a doctor's limited personal space comes with a mountain of chores, but regardless, the two of you have found a new path for a once-stray soul.
Well, seems like a day made for taking a friend's advice, don't you think?

With the New Solar Celebration concluded, Luuk Herssen has stayed true to his word and taken a well-earned vacation. To mark the start of his break, he has prepared a fresh batch of waffles and invited you over.
How will the new waffles taste, and is the doctor getting along with his new feline roommate? Head to the Infirmary to catch up with Luuk Herssen.

Accustomed to the wild, the kitten struggled to adapt to life in a small room. It was born free-spirited. Yet even a soul like that needs a place to rest, and Luuk Herssen has become a quiet harbor where it can occasionally drop anchor. For him, this seems to be the most satisfying outcome.
Under the warm sunlight, you and Luuk Herssen finish your afternoon tea, marking the peaceful beginning of his holiday.
Life is short. We must cherish every encounter.
Where is she?
Like a solitary boat, moored between you and the vast sea of people.

Sigrika returns to her room. 
Her moments of vulnerability in the Academy's Dark Side replay on a loop in her mind. Her cheeks burn with embarrassment. Even hugging her favorite plushie can't stop the blushing.
(This is so humiliating... No, Sigrika! You have to apologize to Senior and the others who were worried about you.) 
With that thought, she opens your chat window on WavesLine.

Your meeting leaves Sigrika in high spirits. You accept her gift—an origami black cat she painstakingly made following a tutorial—and that brings her a great sense of relief.
(Great job, Sigrika! Now, keep that momentum going...)
She pats her cooling cheeks and runs toward the training grounds, leaving a trail of lighthearted notes in her wake.
Folding a black cat out of paper... So difficult...

Sigrika is practicing tirelessly at the training grounds, striving to sketch every rune with absolute precision. 
The weight of everyone's expectations propels her forward, but her nerves have stretched thin, tense as a bowstring pushed past its limit. Even so, she presses on, unaware that her stubborn determination is pushing her toward a suffocating mire...

After her training ends, Sigrika sends you an invitation. She has decided to take you to a place she's always kept to herself—her "secret base."
A seemingly ordinary rooftop is her sanctuary for wandering thoughts and her haven within the Academy. Now, she shares this sacred space with you, hoping you will share this moment with her.
Training is tough, but it's worth it! I'll keep doing my best!

Sigrika leads you to a certain rooftop within the Academy. To any passerby, it looks completely ordinary. But only she knows just how many "spirits of freedom" love to pause and rest on this unassuming place. Every bird visiting the area carries its own character, but their size makes them easy to miss. Spotting them takes a sharp eye. She has one, undoubtedly. And so do you.

You and Sigrika spend the time photographing the birds together. It's something she loves to do, though she admits she usually misses the moment they face the camera. Fortunately, she has you this time. You capture several perfect shots and gift one to her.
Carrying Sigrika's quiet hopes for freedom, the birds lift into the horizon and disappear into the endless blue.
Senior, do you like birds?

Sigrika sits in silence on the rooftop. 
The wind, which once brought her endless inspiration, now only brushes past her, stealing her warmth. Her heart of gold has grown heavy, each beat a soft whimper.
Please, stop crying out, she prays, but it is to no avail. 
Just then, Sigrika hears the sound of your footsteps.

Catching a moment when you aren’t looking, Sigrika's eyes drift to the hem of your sleeve.
She has always told herself she can't run away—because of everyone's expectations, because of her own pride… Yet you never say those words. You simply tell her she's allowed to step back. To rest.
Slowly, the tension starts to ebb, and her heart stops its soft whimpering.
The wind quiets down, and a bird lands gently at your side.
Senior, can you stay with me a little longer?

With the Dark Side crisis resolved, Sigrika is in higher spirits than ever before. After rushing to share her joy with you, she heads back to her sanctuary, her heart still racing with excitement. 
This place has witnessed her expectations, her fragility, and her confusion. Now, it finally holds her happiness. As she tells the birds and the horizon the story of your journey together, she makes a silent vow to cherish these memories forever.

Sigrika returns to her room.
Her brilliant adventure in the Academy's Dark Side replays on a loop in her mind. Her cheeks burn with heat. Even after running several laps around her room, she can't get the temperature to drop.
(I'm so, so happy. Sigrika, you did it!)
With that thought, she opens the photo of the two of you. Her heart of gold, light once more, continues to dance with joy.
I'll treasure our photo! I'll keep it right beside my other most precious ones.
"Festivals Don't Encore"

The New Solar Celebration belongs to the students, not the faculty keeping order, and certainly not the president overseeing it all. You've grown used to Lucilla's packed schedule. That one movie you watched together seemed to be the only leisure she could steal. But today, just outside the venue, you spot her looking remarkably relaxed...
"How's that for a teaser?"

As the Academy President, Lucilla is well aware of the sources of her students' stress, and this stroll is a moment of respite stolen from her own hectic schedule. After a brief chat, she returns to her duties, leaving only a promise to watch a movie together next time.
Will she truly be able to find the time to keep the promise?
"Treat it as a plot hook, one to be revealed when you meet again in the next 'scene.'"
"Take time out for those things that really make you happy, like watching a movie..."
"Department of Engineering Repair Scene"

On a day that started out like any other, you receive an unexpected message. The mere fact that the ever-busy Lucilla reached out at all is a rarity in itself. She brings two pieces of bad news: one concerns you, and the other... well, that concerns you, too.
"If a movie trailer were written this way, I'd accuse the PR department of being lazy. Then again, some of the best films start exactly the same way."

While helping Lucilla retrieve a repaired projector, you catch a glimpse of her life beyond the role of president—her side as a teacher. A top scholar of the Pioneer Association, a mentor to her students... Lucilla spins gracefully between her various roles, executing every footwork of the dance perfectly. 
"Alright, you, stop daydreaming. Let's move on to the next episode."
(A silent, elegant, and precise rhythm, as if it is dancing.)
"Life of a Resonator"

Even with her schedule packed to the brim, Lucilla still made time to point you toward the Academy's finest view.
Gardens are often where stories unfold—be they horror or romance—but on this campus, the faculty ensures they remain strictly for relaxation. Head to the garden and admire the greenery so meticulously tended to by the support staff. 
"Awaiting my message? I'm afraid I really am swamped this time."

Lucilla has hit a snag trying to pick the right film. She invites you to help her navigate the "vast sea of movies" to find the perfect one.
Head to the library and pick out a film that catches your eye. 
"The movies we love are always connected to us in some way. Sometimes the link sparks an instant memory. Other times, it's like dust on a film reel, hidden in shadows the naked eye can barely perceive."

You and Lucilla sift through film after film, synopsis by synopsis. She offers a few personal favorites. But for one reason or another, none of them quite make the cut. In the end, both of you agree to watch the tape repaired by the Department of Engineering the next time you meet.
"To have not a single film worth watching... That is truly the audience's darkest hour."
"We, and I say we because I consider you such, must remain lucid to the bitter end."
"Life is Beautiful"

After a long period of relentless work, Lucilla has finally carved out a good stretch of time off. Before the next busy season sweeps in, she seizes the chance to fulfill her old promise: watching that long-delayed film with you.
"Time waits for no one. The final screening begins now!"

You and Lucilla meet in the auditorium. But before the first frame can flicker to life, the projector—Lucilla's faithful companion for years—breathes its last and refuses to play. During the idle chat that follows, you bring up Laurene. After much hesitation, it seems she has finally made her choice. How many times does one really get to choose in a lifetime? Those who have not yet reached the end can never know. All they can do is hold onto hope.
"Please stay tuned for the next story."

At the edge of the Dim Forest, a narrow cave beckoned with a low rumble and whistling wind.

Nightmares from the depths of dreams loom in the "Memory of Deathmatch," bringing corruption to the dreamer's mind. Enemies will be exceptionally dangerous, and the Resonator will sustain damage every second.
In certain aberrant Memory Zones haunted by vile thoughts in the dreamscape, enemies become exceptionally dangerous, and defeating them grants powerful Metaphors.

Once a trial ground in the coming-of-age ceremony to test the participants' strength. Over time, it has evolved into a place of blessing and prayer for the Sentinel. Pass the trial and prove yourself qualified to protect the Sentinel and Hongzhen.

To safeguard its treasures, the underground of Averardo Vault is designed as an intricate labyrinth, where one might forever lose their way without proper guidance. 
Should fortune, or perhaps misfortune, lead you to its depths, the ever-watchful Echo guard will be there, standing vigilant to fulfill its duty.

The Temporal Loop, an arena of destiny, beckons for you again.
The deity that wields heavenly might patiently awaits a fated battle.

A desolate land where time flows chaotically. Guided by the Blazing Feather, with the universe as the chessboard and stars as the pieces, the chosen one reaches out to touch the distant past beneath the Eternal Blaze.

The distorted copy of the painting has created a realm of illusion through the artist's Forte. Her deeply rooted negative emotions have corroded its colors and brought powerful Tacet Discords to life.

The Public Security Bureau has set up this room to resolve civil conflicts. Here, disputing parties can debate, mediate, and negotiate, making conflict resolution more efficient and occasionally assisting in major case investigations.

[About]

After a decade of anticipation, the long-awaited Carnevale has reignited a fiery passion that refuses to fade.

The Water City has just unveiled a corner of its secrets. Now is the best time to set sail, ride the winds, and venture into the uncharted corners of this mysterious land.

With the world's curtain lifting, a new exploration calls—why wait? Dive into the adventure now!

[Eligibility]

Reach Union Level 22 and unlock Utility: Flight.

[Event Rules]

1. During the event, you can invite other players to join the Overdash Challenge in Co-op Mode. The first to finish is the winner.

2. Once the first player finishes, the challenge enters a 20-second final sprint phase. After the sprint phase ends, results will be finalized.

3. Combat is disabled during the challenge. Players must follow the markers to finish the challenge.

4. The final points consist of two parts: Course Completion Points and Ranking Points:

I. Course Completion Points are earned by reaching designated checkpoints along the track.

II. Ranking Points are earned based on the order in which players finish.

To the twelve valiant souls who laid down their lives to shield Septimont from disaster.
 
Were it not for your courage in the face of the Kerasaurs' threat, we would have perished beneath their claws.
 
Out of reverence for your will, we have shrouded your names and identities, erecting this sword tomb to ensure your sacrifice is never lost to the ages.
 
We shall forever remember you. And so, we who were saved by your valor make this vow:
 
Should the Kerasaur rise again to threaten Septimont, we, or our descendants, shall rise to meet it. We shall defend this land as you once did, carrying forth your spirit.
 
This oath shall endure, untarnished by time.

With banners high, let winds arise, and bear me far from all.

From the blood-stained water dripping from my brother's blade,

The dark tides shall never bring thy end!
Gryphon's Fortress, O Gryphon's Fortress, in the unsetting sun you gleam,
Forever kissed by whispering breeze, like an eternal dream.

"You're not Archid. Excuse me, sir, you are…?"

"A TD Outbreak. He saved the people of a village, but didn't have time to save himself. I was all too late."
"On behalf of the Black Shores, I offer our deepest respect and condolences to this Consultant."

"You wish to take on his duties?"

"I'll stay here. For someone like me, a Gladiator who's lost everything, a glorious death is the best I could ask for."

Annals of Past Primuses (Volume One, Excerpts)

The Founding Primus, Napoli the Second

Being the first leader chosen by the Sentinel to bear the Orchestrate carrying Their power, Napoli the Second was the commander who brought an end to the War of Faith, restoring both unified belief and territory to the people of Rinascita.
His ten-year reign brought legal reforms that standardized Rinascita's confused patchwork of laws. Furthermore, by the Sentinel's will, he also oversaw the propagation of the "Common Echoes," designed to shepherd the people back towards a life of normalcy. Under his watch, the Council of Ten was established to balance and legislate between the interests of nobility and common folk.
However, the exhaustive task of laying Rinascita's very foundations ultimately claimed this remarkable Primus. He did not live to see Rinascita grow to its full potential (a point of contention to this day).

The Gilded Primus, Clement

Clement, the sole Primus to hail from the Fisalia bloodline, led the formal codification of the Order's doctrines with the help of the Fisalias. Backed by his family's immense wealth, he elevated the Order's reach and influence to new heights. However, his mental stability deteriorated in later years, leading to erratic attempts to alter the fundamental doctrines—until his unexpected death.
Official historiography attributes his demise to undisclosed and secretive Fisalia rituals. Yet, whether his fractured mind was a consequence of these rituals or the influence of other dark forces remains a compelling subject of discussion.

The Technocrat Primus, Vester the First

A visionary who placed great faith in scientific progress, Primus Vester the First spearheaded the continuous development of Common Echo technology.
His most enduring achievement was the refinement of frequency editing, which lowered the time necessary to bridge the residual frequencies of Tacet Discords and solidified the Order's control over the long-range aggregation technology. For the first time, all Order-operated Common Echoes within Rinascita were able to maintain a state of perpetual frequency aggregation.
This achievement rendered the routine recall and destruction of Echoes obsolete, except in special circumstances. It was a major leap in overcoming the spatiotemporal constraints on Common Echoes and greatly enhanced their stability.

The Carnevale Primus, Pettini

A ruler of extraordinary openness and tolerance, Pettini ushered in an era of unprecedented prosperity. Society flourished, marked by remarkable advancements in technology and philosophy. Yet, as the constraints of tradition fell away, the people plunged into recklessness. With their faith eroded, they started to question the Divinity. What began as enlightenment devolved into dissension.
Thus, Pettini became the architect of ruinous revelry. Over time, the reformists rose in opposition and stripped him of the Primus Seat.
Shortly before his death, Pettini uttered these heretical words: "The Order of the Deep is already a swamp. The statutes, the deeds, the words—they are all twisted. We are beyond salvation... so why not just laugh?"

The Reformist Primus, Podolisk

Primus Podolisk personally executed his predecessor, whose reign had descended into grotesque decadence. Through this bold action, Podolisk averted the fragmentation of Rinascita and guided the people back to the path of unity. He restructured the Council of Ten into the Order Tribunal and tasked it with mediating civil disputes, prosecuting political crimes, and overseeing public affairs.
In his twilight years, Podolisk enacted sweeping theological reforms that would forever alter some of the Order's doctrine. Where previous teachings had maintained that Sentinel Imperator held a high position among many divine beings, Podolisk declared Imperator to be the one true Divinity. As a result, He issued a decree forbidding Acolytes from venerating any other deities.
The History of Rinascita (Excerpt 1)

The two great families diverged on the question of whether a formal faith should be established for the Sentinel.

The Fisalias argued that Rinascita must not retread the fate of the fallen archipelagos and could no longer endure fragmented governance. They advocated for a unifying faith to guide its people, with the Sentinel as the ideal deity. In their view, establishing this faith would also serve as Rinascita's expression of gratitude toward the Sentinel.

Contrasting sharply with this view, the Abrogati warriors held that the Sentinel was a rare and unrepeatable miracle that could not be summoned at will. To place one's hope in a Divinity whose presence is uncertain, they argued, was both foolish and cowardly. The Sentinel had already demonstrated immense benevolence by guiding the people of Rinascita to new lands. To continue praying for further intervention was inapropriate. Instead, they insisted that people must strive to become warriors worthy of standing alongside such a divine being, facing calamity not through supplication, but through strength.

The difference between the two forces steep in historical tensions eventually erupted into large-scale conflict. It was only when Tacet Discords attacked Rinascita that both sides realized their new land was far from a place where they could rest easy.

In the aftermath of the Tacet Discord Crisis and following lengthy negotiations, the Abrogati and their supporters moved westward into the wilds, where they founded Septimont. Meanwhile, the Fisalias led those who remained in establishing what would become Ragunna.
The History of Rinascita (Excerpt 2)

After the Fisalia family established the Sentinel faith and positioned themselves at the core of the religious structure, an increasing number of people in Ragunna began to dream of a fish imbued with divine presence. This phenomenon was especially common among the fishing communities who often went out to sea. When fishermen prayed to this fish in their dreams, their prayers were answered—sometimes with a more bountiful catch, other times by safely avoiding an approaching storm...

These accumulating small miracles over time gave rise to a new faith. While practitioners maintained their devotion to the Sentinel, they increasingly directed prayers to the dreamt fish, drawn by its tangible blessings.

Fearing crackdowns from the Fisalia family, followers of this new faith dared only to spread their belief within a limited circle among the lower classes. Yet as more discovered their shared worship of the same divine fish, a new clandestine group arose.
The History of Rinascita (Excerpt 3)

On the same fateful day, both leaders of the Order, Napoli the First and Napoli the Second, received divine revelations. After deliberation, they agreed that Napoli the Second would embark on a pilgrimage befitting the revelations, while Napoli the First would remain behind to lead the faithful.

In the third year of Napoli the Second's departure, Napoli the First suddenly fell ill and died, leaving the Order leaderless. When the Fisalia family caught wind, a war over authority to interpret the faith was inevitable.

Many believed this conflict would continue indefinitely, but a Dark Tide broke the stalemate. Inexorable in its advance, the Dark Tide indiscriminately overran the homes of all Rinascitans. The Tacet Discords, which surged from the Tides, were so relentless that both warring sides found themselves exhausted and forced into retreat. As each side prepared for a desperate final battle, Napoli the Second returned from his pilgrimage with a sacred lantern-shaped relic which a flood of Divine Envoys emerged, turning the tide of battle.

Following this event, Napoli the Second's prestige soared. Recognizing that their situation was untenable, the Fisalia family initiated peace talks with The Order. The precise details of the negotiation have been lost to time, as only a handful were present when Napoli the Second entered the gate of Fisalia castle, bearing a tightly bound sword.

Following these talks, Napoli the Second's coronation as Primus proceeded without opposition, and governance of Ragunna transitioned to The Order of the Deep.

<s>Fenrico's devotion, wisdom, and determination are sufficient for him to become a second significant Priest in Avenolium.</s>

<s>Unfortunately, compared to the other one, he seems to lack spiritual insight and flexibility…</s>

Impossible, impossible! So long as I study hard and practice what we preach, I WILL stand before the Divinity someday.

Is it not right to take the sacred Codex in its most literal form and apply these truths to every aspect of society?

These teachings are the only authoritative truth. I must still be lacking the full comprehension. But once my understanding is clear enough to uphold these truths, They will surely understand. They will surely see me.

The Divinity is gone with the Blessed Maiden.
Rinascita must have its Divinity.
This... is my chance.
I will sit on that chair.
I will console the flocks.
I will deliver the Divinity's Oracle.
As it should have been my right.

The Carnevale must be canceled to safeguard the authority of our Order and to strengthen the foundation of our faith.

Only then will the Blessed Maiden be gone forever. Without her meddling, I shall lead Ragunna to a better future.

Merely delivering the Oracle is simply insufficient to earn people's trust. I must step back, foment a disaster, and perform an act of salvation.

When this year's liner is sunk by the behemoth monster of the sea, and the tide washes up horrific casualties, they will understand the punishment I speak of. Only then will I call upon divine power to halt the disaster. As the curtain falls on this spectacle, they will see the truth with their own eyes, and in that moment, all will trust me unreservedly. The masses will instead cheer as I cancel the Carnevale.

Welcome to Jinzhou.
Huanglong is made up of the capital and six cities. As the youngest among them, Jinzhou is a key fortress guarding the border, a frontline against Tacet Discords.
Under the blessing of Sentinel Jué and the protection of the Midnight Rangers, Jinzhou has forged a unique cultural character despite its perilous surroundings.
Whether you're just passing through or thinking of calling this place your home, we hope you will enjoy your time in Jinzhou.
Septimont is so beautiful... People drinking their fill, laughing their hearts out. So unrestrained, so full of life.
Laurus Salad is as delicious as ever. And the wheat juice here is quite good, too... heheh.
Before the High Tide surges in the hunting grounds, let's take a moment to enjoy this moment.
Hear that? The cool breeze through the golden flags and wind chimes… that gentle, beautiful ring.
I've already submitted a full report on everything that happened at the Fabricatorium of the Deep.
Had to pull some overtime to get it done… but it was worth every minute.
After all, this is a major issue. It concerns the safety of all Rinascita.
Don't worry. Go ahead and investigate over in Septimont.
Ragunna has us on its side.
My dear friend, have you made it to the campfire at the hunting grounds?
This victory belongs to every one of us.
I'm still turning over what must come after.
Yes, I can feel the energy in the air.
Yes... I'm still turning over the matter of the Sentinel's Relic.
Take it easy. Rest well, and you'll find the strength to head back into the fray.
The firelight reflects the trust between us. Only when we stand together will the banner of Septimont stand tall forever.
No matter what dangers lie ahead, know that you may contact me at any time.
I would not miss a single chance to fight beside you.
The honey wine I drank beneath that triumphant rain of petals was the sweetest I've ever tasted.
Is it because we came back from the brink of death?
Is it because...
Is it because we've just emerged from the Chaos between life and death, between existence and oblivion?
Hmm. I didn't think I could still drink Septimontian honey wine one day.
Don't tell me it's simply because it was poured by yours truly?
Heh... You might be right.
With every sip, I can feel myself existing again. Even though "fate" never did sign off on this moment...
To hell with it! Let's go overturn more destined futures together, Unwritten!
Since leaving the Black Shores, I'm still the same as ever. Seeking. Chasing. Hunting...
But my state of mind isn't the same as it was before...
Maybe it's because of this Blake Bloom on my shoulder...
It reminds me I'm not alone anymore.
The ship carrying us away is steadier than the one that brought us here.
The sea is calm. Good for quieting the mind.
The threat of the Dark Tide is gone, and our rebuilding efforts are now mostly complete.
Ragunna and Septimont will forever remember what you did for us.
Looks like I'll be spending some extra time at the Black Shores and in Honami City.
Let's treat this as a little vacation before we head back to campus, okay?
Namipon says there are still a lot of unresolved issues here in Honami.
If you're interested, we could look into it.
Of course, we'll do it together.
Frequency reading complete. Access privileges confirmed.
Welcome home, {PlayerName}.
When the moon is full, the roving one returns...
You really are the "One Who Returned." And together, we did slay that monster. We fought our way through the long night and emerged victorious.
Because of this, Jinzhou is safe. The spirits of the Midnight Rangers can finally rest easy... both those who fell in this battle and those lost in the Retroact Rain three years ago.
I will continue to stand guard over Norfall Barrens. I will protect this land we defended together.
That is my duty. And it is how I thank you.
Changli invited {PlayerName} and Jinhsi to the group chat.
Fellow traveler, honored guest, Arbiter... With so many titles, what should I call you?
Your call. Anything's fine.
{PlayerName}.
Call me whatever you like.
Just call me {PlayerName}.
Heh, after what we just went through together… I believe we're close enough to call each other by name.
{PlayerName}, at Mt. Firmament… thank you for stepping in.
It's all thanks to Jinhsi for buying us the time.
It's all thanks to the Wayfinder for guiding us to the end.
You and Jinhsi have both done so much.
If Jinhsi hadn't risked everything in that fight, neither Mt. Firmament nor Jinzhou would have survived this.
If you hadn't guided us through the maze, we'd have been lost forever in those tangled Temporal Disruptions.
I merely showed the way. Our span of life is heaven's decree... There is no need to brood.
This wasn't my sole achievement. You and Jinhsi have both worked hard.
Time fell into disarray, the firmament stood still... Yet a single candle's flame managed to set the heavens alight.
The Magistrate staked her life in this struggle to correct the flow of time, and at last wrested a sliver of hope for Jinzhou...
It needed to be done.
Now that time is flowing again, we can once more feel Jinzhou's clear spring days and its snowy winters...
{PlayerName}, would you stay here a little longer?
There are still so many beautiful places in Jinzhou. Once I've fully recovered, I want to visit them with you.
I hope you'll take care of yourself in the meantime, Jinhsi.
Perhaps these cold lines of text cannot carry the warmth of sunlight.
But please, keep seeking the starlight that binds the world together.
I will stay here, on this shore, guarding everything you once left behind.
Thank you, my Shorekeeper.
Please continue to listen for the rising tides.
If you can connect to Tethys, it might make things easier for you...
All in all… From now on, let me share the road with you.
With the Carnevale about to begin, Ragunna—the Nation of a Thousand Islands, the City of Echoes—warmly welcomes every visitor.
Please adhere to the Order of the Deep's rules while taking in Ragunna's unique charm.
May Sentinel Imperator be with you.
Here, glory is forged. Welcome to the City of Gladiators—Septimont!
In the name of glory, fear no death... The Great Agon is now in full swing!
If that piques your interest, be sure to head over to the arena and experience the thrill of the Agon for yourself.
May applause greet the warriors who've come from afar!
At the Carnevale, we pulled off a damn near perfect performance.
I'm in no rush to end our fun just yet... How about a couple of drinks? I've made you a very special concoction.
Let the revelry continue!
On my way!
We'll be waiting for you in the cafeteria.
One more thing. As for what concerns you, I've already had my family begin investigations.
If I learn anything, I'll be sure to contact you. We'll plan our next moves accordingly.
Oh yes. And should anything stand in your way while in Ragunna City, you need only to invoke the Montelli name. I've got your back.
Cartethyia has found herself again, and the Fisalias have their freedom.
All of this is thanks to you, {PlayerName}.
Aside from the Bloodpact's Pledge, if there is something else you want... come find me at Porto-Veno Castle.
Hmm... what shall I arrange for you? A full spread of the Fisalia's signature tea, or perhaps a private ball, spun straight from a dream…
You'll find out when you get here.
This is my duty, but...
Right now, I wonder if I might modify this messaging Terminal.
Let's not burden Tethys System with this.
No, no, this is fine. Talking like this still feels like I'm talking with you in person.
I see. Then I suppose it's fine then.
Excuse me, {PlayerName}. A moment of your time, please.
We're running a new testing phase for the research project you previously participated. Are you interested in joining us again?
I'm interested.
I'm not interested.
Great. Allow me to introduce our research once more.
No need to decline just yet. Allow me to introduce our research once more.
I'm sure you have experience with Instructor Yhan's simulated training grounds.
It's where our warriors go to train against holograms of enemies and improve their combat skills.
A while back, the Academy began testing an improved "projection" technology to simulate even stronger enemies.
If the technology is proven effective, we can provide more comprehensive training for our soldiers. This means better results for their overall needs.
We managed to make significant technical breakthroughs from the previous test, but many minute details still need ironing out.
Would you be willing to test it out for us and help with our research again?
Leave it to me.
What am I getting paid?
Any longtime client benefits?
I knew I could count on you.
The access to the simulation is right beside me. Best of luck to you.
Rest assured, having been our top participant in the previous testing, your efforts will be supported by the best resources the Academy has to offer.
The access to the simulation is right beside me. Trust me, the rewards will not disappoint.
The data from this experiment looks positive as well...
About the Academy's research project...
Hi {PlayerName}. Have you given our latest technology a whirl yet?
Yes, I have.
Not yet.
Everyone back at the lab was really excited when they heard you would be assisting our research again.
With your assistance, I have faith that our technology will soon reach its full potential for our soldiers to utilize.
Ah, please remember to go check it out at some point. I've already signed up for you.
Everyone back at the lab was really excited when they heard you would be assisting our research again.
The gateway to the Somnoire is open again… Did something happen?
Ah, there you are! I owe you my thanks for helping us clean up the mess.
Were you intercepting those dream fragments?
Exactly. Those dream masses broke apart into countless dream fragments.
They scattered like leaves in a forest, making it difficult to retrieve them all.
The Ebony Gatekeeper mentioned he's working on a solution.
Is that so? Well, I guess he would've been more suited for this task than me...
Dreamwalker, I have a favor to ask. Can you continue to restore those chaotic Memory Zones?
Do you need to ask?
Sure, as long as you pay me.
Haha, I figured you'd say so! Thank you. And, as always, I'll be there if you need anything from me.
Rest assured. The Somnoire has always been generous. And, as always, I'll be there if you need anything from me.
A familiar view, but without its luster...
Sigh. Such a shame.
Sigh. Such a shame. This is far from enough for this picture book...
What's it for?
Oh, it's you, {PlayerName}. Here's to a world of discoveries and wonders!
What do you think? There aren't any colors yet, but I think the sketches alone are already extraordinary!
Like the work of an exceptional artistic talent.
I picked it up from a merchant I met on the streets. According to him, this book had the potential to become a masterpiece.
But the painter became seriously ill and passed away before applying the colors. No one wants to pay for something incomplete.
The beauties of the landscapes are already preserved by perfect lines, yet lacking the colors to complement them. Such a shame... And here I am, on a search for the right painter to finish the work.
Have you found one yet?
Sounds like a good plan.
No, not yet. But before that, there's something I must take care of first. Do you remember the Overflowing Palette?
Well, as an observer, I shall find a way to continue the book's flow of life.
But before I find this painter, there's something I must take care of first. Do you remember the Overflowing Palette?
Overflowing Palettes can affect colors around them, making them fade in reality.

And it has occurred to me that many of the landscapes sketched inside this picture book have fallen under the influence of these "Palettes." Without their real-world counterparts as references, finding an artist is pointless.
I can help with that.
Count me in that observer gang.
Would you really? Oh, that would mean a great deal to me, {PlayerName}! Then I shall leave the task of restoring the Faded Zones to you.
I'll compile a list of the Faded Zones and send it to you shortly.
Here's to a world of discoveries and wonders.
What made you join the Pioneer Association?
About the "picture book."
Why did I join the Pioneer Association? Out of curiosity, of course. I still remember the words written on the inside cover of Wutherium Geographic.
"Go see the world and witness history in the making. Go see humanity's masterpieces—our art, our buildings, our innovations. Go see it all, and feel it all."
I wish to extend my view far beyond where my body can take it.
Yes. After every Faded Zone is restored, finding a reliable artist to fill in the colors is all we need to do.
Speaking of artists, got anyone that comes to mind, {PlayerName}?
I know an artist friend in Jinzhou.
That's great. Mind introducing me to your friend if you get the chance?
I must return to camp...
I will not lose to some prophecy. I will not...
Fate can be rewritten...
And I shall prove it...
Glad you're alright, Sister! I knew it, you really do get what you pay for!
Dosos, have you calmed down now?
Presley... I lost, I admit it. I'm just so glad you're alright.
The inscriptions on the shield read: Property of Nolon. Use if needed—Fictro not included! You doodle on my shield again, and I'll beat the Dark Tide out of you!
The inscriptions on the inside of the helmet read: May you be swift as the wind. May you be as brave as blazing fire. Happy birthday, sis!
The inscriptions on the spear's shaft read: Chill out already. From yours truly, Fictro the Idiot.

The dagger on the left has forty markings on it, likely representing the number of Dark Tide creatures its owner has hunted.
The dagger on the right has only nine with inscriptions below reading: Times I kicked Fictro's arse.
How do you know me...? Are you a Gladiator?
We've just sent out an emergency assistance request. There's been an abnormal Dark Tide surge. We need reinforcements at the Wastelands!
Cato and Aeolus are pinned down over there, and my squad can't link up with them. We... I...!
Just leave it to me, Fictro.
Don't worry, Fictro. The cavalry's here.
Good... That's good.
I think I got the wind knocked out of me. I, uh, I need to take a breather.
Nolon. Maylia. Dosos. Presley... I've finally... I've finally got us reinforcements...
Grandmother Lillibet... Fate can be rewritten...

Request Order Priority: Critical
To: Fictro Reserve Squad
The Den has detected abnormal Dark Tide fluctuations. Two Gladiators are trapped. Proceed immediately to the marked location to assist.
May howls of triumph follow you, Gladiators.
No... I can't fall here...
I'm a Gladiator... a damn Gladiator... hunting fate...
Nolon? Is that you? I'm sorry I scratched your shield...

(Through the light veil of destiny, I saw a battlefield. There was no smoke in the air, no sound of war drums, no brothers or sisters in arms. This individual will face an unbeatable adversary alone in the twilight of his life...)
Lady Lillibet?
(Aeolus, his eyes burning with desires for glory, but the future revealed by fate is far from what he envisions. He will die in obscurity.)
Aeolus, I see a trial in your future.
A trial... My strengths, my character, have already failed me in trials too many... Lady Lillibet, will I perish in this trial?
We cannot escape death, but we are given the choice on how we should face it.
