Fate casts a stone into the river of time, and every ripple marks the path of your journey around destiny. {0}-{1}-{2}—on this ordinary yet special day, your past, present, and future selves cross paths for a fleeting moment. And now, <color=#fa601a>who might be the one standing before you?</color>

As the sounds in your memory fall into place, their magnificent echo crosses eons to reach your ears. Throughout your journey, your identity and purposes slowly piece themselves back together, and once again, you, the Astral Modulator, return to the center stage.

Wind, though invisible in form, can be seen through the flowers it blows, the flames it caresses, and the larks it makes soar. Wind carries the birdsong high, echoing, echoing... until it is heard once more.

"The Flame Ranger still chooses to challenge an opponent who is simply unbeatable..."
The girl behind the curtain waves a hero figurine in her hand. Whether it was the light or something else, the figurine shone brightly in her grasp.
A bloom in snow is cold yet irresistibly tempting to touch. But in the end, it cannot escape the natural order of things, and melts away in your hand.

A girl who walks among the righteous and the wicked must constantly refine her sense of justice and morality. It is precisely because of this, that the jade pendant hanging from her chest remains so clear and pure.
"Sit, breathe, and find inner peace." She opens her eyes to perceive the gradual stabilization of frequencies, using pupils corroded by Tacet Discords. She had walked away, free from the blizzard.

Being half a step slower also meant that Taoqi had more time to observe the world. She gradually began to notice subtle changes in the marketplace. A brick was missing here. A flower had wilted there. The next season would arrive when she was aware.

Many people light fires they cannot hope to contain.
But he is the creator of fire, the master of fire, and the smotherer of fire.

They say Yuanwu can best any challenger in three minutes. It takes him one minute to step into the ring, then another minute to perform a ceremonial bow, and one final minute before the kettle comes to a boil.
"Come now, all martial artists are friends. Do stay for a cup of tea."

In the market, Aalto floats on the boundary between buying and selling, playing different roles: investor, opportunist, and market mover. He lays chips in every corner.
Every investment made is an avenue of future wealth.
Planting seeds, watering and nurturing them till they sprout and bloom... That's how Verina initially imagined what the process of "Healing" meant.
Encore's paradise is in the land of imagination. Brave Wooly Warriors and their wooly companions leap from the pages of books to a "Happily Ever After."

The "hound" in the shadow stalks his prey. First, he is calm, waiting for his target to move through the crowd. Then, unease sets in as the surroundings grow eerily quiet. Finally, the fangs are bared, and the target can no longer see its own shadow.
With every step a dance, he will surely leap to the highest perch.
With a limpid mind and sustained inner peace, she, who has undergone the trials of the world, completes the final piece of the mirror. The heart is a mirror. The mirror reflects her heart.
"The enemies surging in were suddenly met by a streak of blue light. Qingloong swept in with the wind, and after the storm subsided, the Midnight Rangers' flag stood tall on the high ground…"
Like a puppet with a thousand faces, she walks through the shadows in different facades. But at the end of the day, she's still the one holding the strings.

It was an age when the flow of time was chaotic, with dawn blurring into dusk and the cold proving relentless.
Doubt, weariness, and the weight of duty... such was the life of a Magistrate. Though quite young, she shouldered it all as she ascended the mountain, striving to illuminate the sky with a sliver of candlelight. It was the moment when winter relented. The thaw came, and the slopes awoke, bathed in the first tender hues of spring...

Changli wishes for an era of peace and prosperity.
This is the longest game of Weiqi she's ever played, and with each move, she becomes a part of the game, an eternal fire that lights the way.

Xiangli Yao often describes himself as a greedy person, who is hungry for truth, yet equally starves for the warmth of human bonds.
Though he often gazes at the stars, he occasionally casts glances at the distant mountains and the vast land they anchor. And with each step forward, he measures the distance he has traveled, the life he has lived.

She prefers colors on ink and wash, which, while not the most dazzling, still depict a stunning array of hues.
This is Zhezhi's true colors, that which she hopes will one day burst forth with the power to leave others in awe.
Or at least, during self-introductions...

Starlight falls into the deep sea, filling all of her longing and emptiness. In vastness and loneliness, she stood watch over the shores that exist only because of {Male=him;Female=her}... This is her innate duty, both past and future.
Though young, Youhu can already distinguish real antiques from fakes. Valuables weighed down by time can only be cherished and cared for when entrusted to those who understand their value.
Blossom, wither, and bloom again with memories of the past. When red and white converge... What form will Camellya take when she flowers once more in your eyes?

We Promise, We Deliver!
Bright and cheerful Lumi travels across the vast land of Solaris, delivering messages from distant places to those on her route.

Before this radiant moment arrived, the "gem" had endured endless nights of rain.
Once, she loathed the downpower, but now she embraces the rhythm... With patient hands, she polished the rough stone that was "herself" until it shimmered with a thousand captured hues, in the name of Montelli, and more so in the name of Carlotta.
How should the stage be set for a drama? Spotlights check, curtains check, magnificent costumes? Check. "Pero Pero!" A strange box jumps up and hands her a confetti gun. "Ta-da!" —It's showtime!

Set sail! The curtain rises! This maritime stage belongs to Brant. From the bow comes the scent of "Troupe Strength" and wild laughter mocking the outdated doctrines of The Order. On deck, they're rehearsing plays banned by The Order. From the stern, the sea chases after them in pursuit.

"As the sand of time flickers through your finger, please remember: in the gentle starlight, among beautiful waves, beneath the lantern... and where the kindness of your heart shines, my unspoken words are waiting for you... Listen! The door is open. It's time to move on."

Where does the dream end and reality begin? The moment your fingers meet the jellyfish, you're falling into a deep sea, descending ever deeper... Only to surface at last into the calm harbor of her gaze.

Listen! The chimes of a starry, starry night, a prelude to the young maid's song. Bright as midsummer sun even in the depth of the night, yet gentle as the breeze on a summer's day. The wind carries her music across the dark, a melodic story that greets the dawn.

A fixed routine isn't that bad. Stability has got to count for something. These are words Zani lives by.
Her routine consists of work, meals, sleep, and the occasional bouts of saving the world. Life, after all, is simply a matter of style.

Former senior agent of Mingting's Internal Security Agency. 

Though enmity filled his younger days, loyalty defined his later years. However, scapegoated for a murder, he is now but a blind swordsman wandering the world alone.

Miscellaneous Records of <te href=260009>Mingting</te>'s Minister of Sentinel Affairs: Correspondence Collection

My dear friend Dongyuan,

A few days prior, the <te href=260001>Internal Security Agency</te> forwarded documents from the Justice Commission and the Huaxu Academy to the <te href=260002>Ministry of Sentinel Affairs</te>. Without delay, I instructed the Chongzhou official to assist in the matter and thoroughly examine the local Resonator register. It has now been confirmed that the individual in question has no connection with the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> or the <te href=850074>Threnodian</te> of Chongzhou.

According to the Ministry's records, this individual has been a Resonator for over fifteen years. Described as one who "sees the world through bamboos and hides his blade within them," he is blind yet wields a remarkable ability known as <te href=260003>Mindsight</te>. Through this power, he perceives his surroundings through a "bamboo forest" in his mind, enabling him to discern opponents' intentions and vulnerabilities. He can even manifest the Mindsight into tangible illusions. This is not a person to be underestimated.

Moreover, his swordsmanship appears to stem chiefly from personal skill rather than his Resonance Ability. Observations indicate that he consistently restrains the use of his Resonance power. He claims that the bamboo flask he carries contains a concoction—prepared by a wandering healer in Chongzhou—that stimulates his Mindsight and Forte, and is used only when necessary. This matter may be forwarded to the Academy for further analysis.

As for the detailed test data, please await the Academy's formal report...

Dongyuan's annotation: Simply ensure this is recorded clearly. We follow the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs's judgment… My my, Lin still writes with his characteristic formality.

Miscellaneous Records of Mingting's Ministry of Sentinel Affairs: Correspondence Collection …In my recent observations over the past few days, it appears less that he refuses to employ his Forte and more that he consciously restrains himself from using it. Regarding the nature of the ability itself, he remains decidedly reserved. Only from the Academy's report may one glean a few particulars: Test subject waveform analysis presents an elliptical oscillation. Time-domain readings are stable, with no anomalous patterns observed. Resonant Criticality: High. Stability is high with no risk of Overclocking. No prior history of Overclocking. Psychological intervention is deemed unnecessary. Note: The subject admits to repeated offenses involving violent breaches of the law, though his demeanor was notably composed. It is recommended that these claims should be verified by the Ministry of Justice and local authorities in Chongzhou. …Yet, in my own assessment, this man harbors no murderous intent. His composure is unwavering, his demeanor steady. His swordsmanship is among the finest, and few in all of Mingting could rival him. He could have been a remarkable asset to the Internal Security Agency. That such an individual is listed in the Justice Commission's dossiers as a perpetrator of unlawful violence is difficult to believe. I have already communicated with the Ministry of Rites, outlining the advantages and implications of recruiting said individual. Should you wish to employ this man, I expect no obstacle shall arise on that account. Dongyuan's annotation: Naturally, the steadier the better. But judging from this report... isn't this lad a little too devoid of emotion?

Black Shores Bloom Bearer Research Report Despite the immense power Ms. Galbrena exhibited after Overclocking—including marked transformation of both appearance and physiology—we nevertheless classify her historical Overclock severity rating as Mild. This assessment must be understood in context: her Resonance Ability was once corrupted by the Dark Tide, leaving her almost entirely depleted of her Resonance Ability. For a Resonator so diminished to achieve Overclocking at all—to move from deficit to surplus, from absence to presence—is nothing short of miraculous. Traditionally, Overclocking has been defined as a state that exhausts the mind and body, signifying the dominance of destructive tendencies over regenerative ones within Resonators. Galbrena's case, however, compels us to reconsider this definition. In her, Overclocking did not manifest as deterioration, but as a signal of rebirth. It suggests that the phenomenon may be closely tied to the will of the Resonator and that, if properly guided, Overclocking could potentially yield constructive outcomes, transforming into a power that Resonators could one day learn to wield with intent. Important Note: All research personnel are strictly prohibited from attempting, by any method, to replicate Ms. Galbrena's Overclocking method. Any such action, once discovered, will result in immediate containment measures.

[Filed by Spacetrek Collective: Startorch Academy Student Records] [Forte Examination Report: RA2326-G] Student Name: Sigrika Synchronist Qualification: Negative Forte Overview: Tests reveal a Rabelle's Curve with a pronounced periodic waveform. Therefore, the student is classified as a Congenital Resonator. Her Tacet Mark is located on her back. According to the pre-admission personal file and the student's own account, the student demonstrates exceptional aptitude in deciphering rune frequencies and converting them into usable power. However, she reports that this ability remains unstable and is highly dependent on her mental state as well as her depth of knowledge regarding particular runes. "In the field of rune deciphering, Sigrika displays a rare talent, one that may pose a significant risk to herself if not treated carefully."

Rabelle's Waveform test sample analysis shows high-amplitude, non-periodic fluctuation patterns. Partial waveform blurring is observed, along with visible abnormal waveforms. Currently, Resonator Sigrika has no history of Overclocking, and her Rabelle's Curve remains stable. Routine psychological counseling is required. "Sigrika is too hard on herself. Honestly, if she just eased up a little, her Resonator stability would improve dramatically." "...Students like her are not uncommon at Startorch Academy. They come in thinking their talent means something. Then they realize that here, it just gives them an edge in a few courses. Nothing more." "Still, I don't want our students to feel defined by grades, talent, or ability. They deserve to see how much more the world has to offer."

Into the Land of Paradox

The Liondance Troupe is gearing up for a new performance. Lingyang invites you out for a meal while scouting potential customers along the way. At the last stop, you learn a food stall owner has been threatened by something called the "Jingle Beast" and a gang known as "The Savages." Moved by his story and a request from the Bei siblings, you expose the gang's scheme, and in doing so, come to learn the secret Lingyang has been carrying. After the lion dance, Lingyang tells you an old legend about the "Jingle Beast"...

A team set to compete in the Jinzhou Riverside Games suffers an accident. You came only to watch, but you invite Jiyan to join you in filling the vacant spot. At the end of the race, the Gulpuffs suddenly erupt into chaos. To find the source of the anomaly, you trace it to a Sonoro Sphere upstream. After a fierce battle, you free the reverberations of Jiyan's fallen comrades from within it...

Several residents of Jinzhou City have gone missing recently. As you investigate, you cross paths with an organization known as the Séance Society, as well as Patroller Yinlin, who is investigating them too. Working in tandem, you and Yinlin set out to uncover the truth behind the group. In the end, you defeat its leader, the Dollmaker, and bring him to justice. Then Yinlin bids you farewell and departs on a new journey of her own.

Changli asks to meet you at the pavilion, and to uncover the Secret of Immortality hidden within an unfinished Weiqi game, the two of you once again venture into Mt. Firmament. Through the machinations of the Fractsidus, the adventurer Wuli, trying to save his lover Fuling, is swept into a Temporal Disruption and survives only because you arrive in time. Within the Sonoro Sphere, you witness Changli's past and recover scattered fragments of your own. After the remaining Fractsidus members are captured, Wuli and Fuling decide to keep chasing distant horizons, and you and Changli play out the final moves of the Weiqi game...

Rumor speaks of an Arcane Artist in Jinzhou whose paintings can come to life. While investigating that artist at a client's request, you meet Zhezhi, who is looking into the same matter. Together, you discover that the mysterious artist, Mingyan, already knows Zhezhi and is being forced to forge her work. Determined to bring the mastermind's crimes to light, Zhezhi confronts the Shanyun Art Exchange in open court. With your support, she wins the argument and exposes the truth...

To find the wish-granting relics from Encore's story, you, Encore, and a young listener named Ying, who holds the treasure map, set out on an adventure together. Along the way, Ying learns that she will never see her mother again, and you discover that this story was a gift Encore's mother left for her. Wanting to give the tale a happy ending, Encore gathers everyone's signature flowers and asks Verina to create the final treasure, fulfilling both her own wish and Ying's. Then you and Encore makes a pinky promise to write new stories together in the future.

A corrupted Stellar Matrix has escaped the Error Cell and may threaten the safety of the Black Shores. To track it down, you need Camellya's help. As the investigation unfolds, the past you shared with Camellya, or rather with "Lady Flora," slowly comes to light. After crossing countless junctures, the two of you find each other again, along with the core of the corrupted Stellar Matrix. You meet Camellya at Veiled Rock, where the many timelines overlap and become one the moment she offers you a flower.

An invitation draws you into the dangerous undercurrents of the Montelli family. To investigate the mysterious death of one of its members, you join forces with Carlotta once more. When the truth is finally stripped bare, it points to the sender of the invitation: Carlotta's uncle, Capollo. Carlotta evades his snare and reunites with you, and together you destroy the plan he had devised with the Order of the Deep. Before parting, Carlotta gives you a Cat's Eye gem...

To lift the spirits of the Pilgrims they rescued, Roccia decides to stage a welcome play and perform "Pegasus" with the troupe. In search of the perfect stage prop, a "star," the two of you return to the Strand, only to become trapped in a maze of fog. At its far end, you discover plushies and the "star" who are looking for their owners. You bring them back to the troupe, and the performance is a success. After the curtain falls, the plushies finally reunite with their owners, and Roccia invites you to join the troupe...

After accidentally winning a wager, you become captain of the Troupe of Fool for a day. You and Brant set off in search of lost treasure and cross paths with the greedy pirate Aldric. At the heart of the hidden treasure, Brant sticks to the plan, taking only the sea chart before slipping away with you. Aldric, however, is consumed by his own greed and meets his end. When the adventure ends, Brant tells you the tale of the chart and the Golden Captain. You become the troupe's honorary captain, and the next adventure awaits somewhere on the horizon.

Guided by a message carrying a strange frequency, you arrive in Egla Town and join Cantarella for the Night of Remembrance. When you retire to the Porto-Veno Castle to rest, past and present begin to overlap within its halls, leading you to the answer behind the festival's riddles: the Divine Trials held by the Fisalia family. With your help, Cantarella returns the girls she once saved during those trials, and the dreamy illusion of the night fades away in a veil of gentle smoke.

The Black Alley and Talos, both destroyed years ago at the hands of the Blazing Nightwalker, suddenly reappear in Ragunna. You begin investigating alongside Zani. In the course of that search, you learn that Zani herself is the Blazing Nightwalker. After a hard-fought adventure, you defeat the current Talos and rescue the residents suffering under her tyranny. Zani then tells you why she became the Nightwalker: to protect the precious, fragile peace of ordinary life. That, she says, is how heroes are born.

Hailing from Ashinohara, the Miko of Flaming Sakura now remains in Lahai-Roi as the last and only member of the Special Response Force.
Futures' Tithe

[Spacetrek Collective: Classified Archive] Interview Dossier: Hiyuki Due to multifaceted considerations, we have foregone a truly comprehensive evaluation of the representative from Ashinohara—the Miko of Flaming Sakura. The majority of the intelligence gathered herein is based on her personal testimony. In the recorder's professional estimation, corroborated through subsequent cross-referencing, she appears to harbor no intention of concealing any information regarding her background. "After all, information regarding the 'Miko of Eternal Flaming Sakura' can be found in just about any Ashinohara elementary school textbook..." According to Hiyuki's own account, the source of her Forte is the "Suzu," a Legacy Talisman worn on her right wrist. Hiyuki describes the Suzu as follows: It grants the bearer the ability to perceive and utilize "future possibilities" of oneself, though it does not allow for direct communication with these "shadows of future possibility." The freezing power she often wields in combat also stems from the "Suzu." "Verified via official Ashinohara reports: The Legacy Talismans are five relics left behind by the Sentinels, distributed among the internal factions of Ashinohara for safekeeping." "Among them, the Suzu is described as granting its bearer the power to 'draw upon the future.'" Consequently, it is determined that the fundamental source of her exceptional combat prowess remains her own inherent skill. However, the "futures" available for her to draw upon are not infinite. Out of concern for her physiological lifespan, aggressive deployment of her abilities is strongly advised against. "Investigation confirms that every Miko of Flaming Sakura has shared a singular cause of death: vanishing from the battlefield without a trace following excessive use of the Suzu."

The subject's Rabelle's Waveform diagram exhibits an elliptical oscillation pattern with a stable Time Domain representation. No abnormal fluctuations were observed. Examination results are determined to be within normal parameters. Current Overclocking threshold is exceptionally high, and subject stability remains robust. There is no risk of Overclocking, and the subject has no prior history of Overclocking. However, a course of psychological intervention is recommended. "This miko... How should I put this..." "Ashinohara textbooks never show her face, but they're clear about one thing. She is the strongest living warrior in all of Ashinohara." "And yet, with all that combat, her readings stay perfectly stable. Something about that just doesn't sit right..." "I get your concern, but the data is clear. There's not a single irregularity." "...Then what about those shadows? Like parallel-universe versions of herself from some movie?" "Hardly. It must be the Suzu's power. Just as the Ashinohara records describe, it allows her to 'draw upon the future' to a certain extent."

Denia, a Department of Voidmatters student at Startorch Academy. Also, a professional slacker who has mastered the art of dozing through courses.
Still, she hardly misses any campus event, always there to flash her "gentle" smile to one and all.

"Wait, isn't that the bubble maker from those Lollo Logistics ads? My niece has that same exact toy! How in the world are you supposed to stop Voidmatter with bubbles like that?" "How did this get filed in the first place?! My goodness... Is anything in this report actually true?"

Before your eyes, the Mourning Aix is reunited with its mate in their final moments. The researcher Jiuyue chooses to carry the memory of a loved one and move forward, and at last, the fog over Whining Aix's Mire is dispersed. This may not be an ending, but rather the beginning of a new story.
You help Shicheng complete the Rite of Offering that has been passed down for generations, and she resolves to carry the tradition forward.
A girl from Hongzhen named Shicheng wishes to perform the Rite of Offering, but she is attacked by TDs. You manage to save her just in time.
You and Shicheng climb to the peak of the arch-shaped rock and complete the rite.
You and Shicheng travel to where the waterfalls converge and complete the rite.
You and Shicheng reach the shoals and islands and complete the rite.
You and Shicheng come to the boundary of yellow and white and complete the rite.
You and Shicheng enter the Offering Site and complete the final rite.

Using the Prototype Chronosorter, you repair the damaged Woodveil Hall, and the once-withered Tianqu Tree springs back to life. Afterward, you tell the relic merchant Chenpi everything that happened here, and the story set in motion by a single ancient artifact finally comes to a close.

To find Liel, the missing companion of the Exile Insula, you enter the Twilight Rise with him. There, you become trapped for a time and are attacked by an unknown monster. You eventually find a way out, but Liel is nowhere to be found.

You then enter the Resounding Rise with Liel's sister, Itzel. There, you encounter the same unknown monster again and discover that the Fanatic Shark gang, responsible for Liel's disappearance, has itself been wiped out by the creature. Within the tower, you uncover the reason the Fisalia family built the Thorncrown Rises. Sadly, Liel still remains missing.

Following the monster's frequency, you, Insula, and Itzel enter the Command Rise and uncover a secret weapon created by the Fisalia family. At last, you catch up with the monster and defeat it, but by then, Liel is already dead. After thanking you for your help, the Exiles decide to leave Rinascita behind.

You complete the trial on the Shores of Last Breath amid raging winds. Though you cannot help but question why the Sentinel and the Order would have set such a test, the truth has long since been buried by history.

The Acolyte Lenore asks you to recover the long-lost Nimbus Chorales. You gather its scattered parts in Nimbus Sanctum, but Lenore believes one final passage is still missing. At that moment, the lost Major Forbidden Archive reappears, and she asks you to enter it in search of the last part.

Deep within the Archive, you recover the missing part, only to find that it does not praise the Sentinel as Lenore expected, but the ancient people of Rinascita. She believes this runs counter to the Order's teachings, yet she is still moved by the emotions carried in the music. Until she can resolve the doubts it has stirred within her, she decides not to report it to the Order.

You, Phoebe, and Zani escort a "relic" entrusted to you by the Order into an unknown area deep within the Averardo Vault. There, you uncover the secret that the Montelli family once sheltered a group of artists and scientists from the Order. Though they are long dead, their Reverberations remain trapped within the vault. At the same time, you realize that the "relic" you brought inside is in fact a bomb the Order intended to use to erase its own crimes. 
Phoebe uses her power to defuse the crisis before anything happens, and with the imprisoned Reverberations finally set free, the vault's great doors swing open once more.

Guided by the Nimbus Wraiths, you free the memory fragments left behind by past candidates of the Divine Trials, and at "Lake of Spirits" you witness a breathtaking meteor shower. Traveling beside you, Cantarella makes a wish that one day the Fisalia family will be freed from the curse of the Threnodian, and that everyone will be able to enjoy life in peace and freedom.

In the ruins near the Ashen Dragon's Crypt, you find the Scourgewing, Iaen, trapped by hunters. From the nearby Reverberations, you learn that a Gladiator named Levis tried to rescue Iaen from them in defense of his honor, only to be trapped himself. In his final moments, Iaen creates an illusion so that Levis may finally lay his regrets to rest in one last duel.
Together with Tulia, you rescue the trapped Scourgewing, Isth, from a tower, and you also witness the undying friendship between fallen members of the Black Shores and Gladiators.

The Scourgewings you saved, Isth and Iaen, soar back into the sky as the wilds once ravaged by the Dark Tide slowly begin to recover. They will fly toward distant lands, while Tulia returns home to continue her research. Though you part for now, as long as you live beneath the same sky, you are certain to meet again.

Pursuing Phrolova's phantom, you descend deep into Mournfell Canyon, where you encounter Lenore and a man calling himself a Reverberation, Medulius. Your investigation reveals that Medulius came here to revel in the "blood duel" he himself set in motion, a father and daughter driven to kill one another, only to be cursed by Phrolova and denied the release of true death. After you defeat the Gladiator father and daughter, as well as Medulius, silence finally falls. You decide to continue the hunt for Phrolova, but are unsuccessful in locating her.

A Kronaclaw corrupted by the Void Storm leads you and its Shepherd, Skavitz, to the ruins of Upphaf Forest. Though already consumed by corruption, it still manages to return there and pour the last of its strength into the Life Chamber core. Under that core's power, the long-since withered forest slowly begins to recover. Spent and powerless, the bird flies off alone and disappears into Upphaf's frozen caverns.

Later, you and Skavitz find the Void Storm corrupted Kronaclaw once more. Unable to return to its flock and unwilling to endanger the others, it follows a Kronaclaw's instinct back to Upphaf Forest, the ancient homeland of its kind. There, you help free it from the torment of corruption. Returned at last to its home, it no longer has to fly alone.

Lenie, one of Warren's students, ventures into a contaminated Voidmatter zone in an attempt to prove herself and falls into danger. When you come to help, the two of you discover the first-generation Helios, a prototype Warren had abandoned years ago. With the help of several professors, you restore it, and Lenie finally finds her own path. She vows never to repeat Warren's mistakes. In the days ahead, she'll live up to her mentors' hopes and strive, like any true researcher, to bring hope and progress to humanity.

Sigrika discovers an ancient ruin still brimming with life. There, you find a very special feather. It leads you to Aurora Bridge, where you free an Auroraclaw trapped in ice. Once freed, the bird carries you and Sigrika into the sky. Beneath its wings, the world opens up below you. Wide, peaceful, and breathtaking.

To find the gift her sister Shiyu left behind, you accompany Shixia through waterfalls and across open wilds on a journey through memories that belong only to her. When Shixia realizes that her sister's "gift" was simply the vast landscape beneath her feet, and a wish for Shixia to move forward bravely, she decides to climb the even steeper West Mountain with you, just as Shiyu once did.

After crossing a harsh mountain path, the two of you reach the top of West Mountain at sunrise. At the summit, Shixia realizes that her sister has always been watching over her and encouraging her. She resolves to face the future with courage.
Back at the theater, Shixia, just like Shiyu before her, encourages a little girl named Mumin to move forward bravely as well.

You set out on an adventure with the plushies of Plushie Village who long to explore the world. Along the way, you take plenty of photos for them. At one point, you even step alone into a strange world inside a painting and capture a one-of-a-kind night sky, unlike anything you've ever seen. Maybe that's what adventure is really about: finding unique sights in faraway places. Your journey inspires the other plushies too scared to leave before. In the end, the plushies who explored with you take a photo of you standing beneath the stars, then quietly add themselves into the picture.

When everything is over, you reunite with Cartethyia at a Septimontian plaza. Though a few regrets remain, she is content with a life in which she can cook the food she loves, travel freely, and meet the people she wishes to see.

After the dust settles, you share drinks with Lupa on the hotel terrace. In the warm evening light, she swears to you, and to the undying sun, that if you ever call for her, she will come to whatever battlefield awaits you.
Near the cable car, you meet Buling just before her holiday ends. Before leaving, she gives you a bronze mirror and says that perhaps the two of you will meet again someday.
You report the situation beneath the sea to Zani, the Black Shores, and Cartethyia, then decide to return to Septimont and investigate the truth behind the "Journeying Paradise."

A Hurriclaw named "Chunkie," corrupted by the Dark Tide while trying to save the old Gladiator Arctos and a little Wootter named "Teeny," keeps circling outside the camp. Together with Arctos, you free Chunkie from the Dark Tide. It scatters into the wind, leaving behind only a feather from Arctos's helmet. Arctos fastens the feather to the tail of the Hornett, hoping that Chunkie's will to protect others will live on in its cry and reach every Gladiator who hears it.

The old Gladiator Aeolus, whom you rescued during a scouting mission in the Wastelands, cannot stop dwelling on the past. He regrets being a coward and leaving Cato to face the Dark Tide alone. He wants to become the man who fought bravely instead. He joins you in killing a Kerasaur near camp, then after losing a sparring match with you, he leaves.

After leaving, Aeolus resolves to hunt a Corrosaurus alone. When you find him and the beast, the two of you defeat it together despite his injuries, but he does not survive. You return to camp bearing news of his death. Standing by his new sword grave, Rolla, who had always stayed by his side, tells him that in her heart, he was always a hero. Not because he chose to fight, but because he chose to save her from the Dark Tide.
A letter Ephor Augusta writes to the Gladiator Aeolus. She still remembers him as a worthy rival and rejects his request to leave the ranks.

You save a dying Aria Mummer and promise to fulfill its final wish by delivering Melody Boxes to the people they were meant for. As you carry them across the city, you witness one small life after another in Septimont. Through the melodies, people come to glimpse sides of their loved ones they never knew. After the last Melody Box is delivered, the Aria Mummer returns to the Resonance Nexus, leaving only a faint strain of music echoing in people's hearts.
The recovery efforts in Rinascita after the Dark Tide leave Phoebe overwhelmed. You decide to help her by taking on some of the work in Septimont.

In the Mournfell Canyon, you meet Acolyte Lenore, the one Medulius once protected. Having returned from the Dark Tide, Lenore is burdened by guilt for having abetted evil and is unsure of what she should do now. With your encouragement, she decides to join the recovery efforts in Septimont and do whatever she can for others.

The rebuilding of Septimont's Old District moves forward smoothly thanks to everyone's hard work. You help Lenore face her fears and meet the Troupe of Fools, once oppressed by the Order, which loosens some of the knots still tied in her heart. In the end, she gives the Nimbus Chorales to the troupe and resolves to stop drowning in self-pity and find a way to keep living.

The celebration marking the completion of the small square begins. Amid joyful music, Lenore steps onto the stage and confesses what she truly wants: to keep helping people. As the Nimbus Chorales rise into the air, the final knot in her heart is released.

At sunrise, the celebration comes to a perfect close. Lenore tells you that when she let go of everything weighing her down and sang freely, she became a Resonator, awakening the power to "heal." She intends to use that gift to help Rinascita heal and do what she believes is right.

Septimont's Old District is showing signs of recovery. There, you see Julia Silva, once exiled and now returned, surrounded by jeering crowds. Ignoring their scorn, she takes her nephew Adric's spear and heads alone into the Mournfell Canyon, swearing to reclaim the Silvas' honor.

You and Lenore witness an argument between Luther and Alessio. Though innocent, Luther chooses not to abandon his colleague Alessio but to stand beside him and be judged by the people together. After they leave, you and Lenore talk about whether Julia and Luther truly deserve punishment. Lenore decides that she, too, must find the courage to change and make amends.

A frail little girl named Misha asks you to help find the Soliskin stickers left by her mother, Vantier. While gathering them, you inadvertently learn that Vantier has already passed away. Having sensed the truth herself, Misha quietly slips away and passes on as well. Like the Soliskin, they will both become light, and in that warmth, they will meet again.

At Zahira's recommendation, you become a test volunteer helping rebuild the route network across the Etching Plains. With Elowyn's assistance, you restore the transport routes, and the lifelines of the plain begin to spread out beneath your feet once more.

Songdis, hopelessly absorbed in games, decides to create 8-bit chiptune music for the Roya. You go with her to Bjartr Woods, where you turn the melodies played by the Soliskin into a new song. With her wish fulfilled, she decides to put games aside for a while and throw herself into her studies, though she will never forget the memories those games and songs gave her.

A student named Ang, who loves stargazing, wants to watch the stars again with his old classmates. You help him invite them, along with Miss Dhalifa, to the Observatory. Beneath a sky glittering with stars, you take a group photo and make a promise: no matter how far apart you may be, one day you will all watch the stars together again.

You take part in the "Light Chaser Collection," a photography event organized by the Photography Fan Club, and use your camera to capture snapshots of student life. When you deliver the photos, the club leader, Lianna, gives you a record in return, hoping that the songs on it will accompany you through this bright and precious chapter of campus life.

A student named Daigo discovers that someone has been impersonating him at the Academy and asks you to track the impostor down. To everyone's surprise, the "Fake Daigo" turns out to be a formal B.1.N.G.O. unit disguised by I.R.I.S. It accomplishes what Daigo never had the courage to do, nudging him to confess to the girl he loves, Nanami, and to join the scientific expedition team. Now Daigo is chasing his dreams together with Nanami.

At the Academy, the renowned Professor Edgar is about to retire. His student, Frantz, wants to send him off with his own research: a grand fireworks display. But your choices, in ways unseen, will decide whether Frantz can make it to Edgar's farewell ceremony in time. When the sky finally erupts with fireworks, Professor Edgar tells him the truth: the man who always considered himself ordinary has, in fact, always been his proudest student.

Robbie, a Mechascout corrupted by the Void Storm and nearing the end of its service life, sets out with you to fulfill its final wishes. One by one, you help it do the small things it never had the chance to try. At the very end, it makes one last gesture. Showing both its love for the world and its longing to fly, it falls from the sky like a meteor, opening its mechanical arms toward the land that meant so much to it.

Together, Dari of the Roya people and you from Startorch Academy, restore the Spacetrek Collective's power supply and relight Roya petroglyphs so they can shine once more beneath Lahai-Roi's sky. Now, illuminated by the Collective's light, the petroglyphs are more than a work of Royan artistry. They have become a symbol of both peoples standing together to protect Lahai-Roi.

You bring Mr. Trevor, now old and unable to travel himself, the photographs you took from within the Void Storm. Though age has kept him from venturing out in person, he still wants to turn those magnificent images into postcards and send them to his friend, Mr. Fulmine, in Ragunna.

To explore whether a different holographic projection is possible, you and Mornye enter the "ocean" projected within the Submerged Tunnel. There, Mornye, who has never seen the ocean with her own eyes, makes you a promise: one day, she will see the real thing in person, with you beside her.

While helping Ero sort through a pile of odds and ends, you accidentally uncover a number of precious pre-Lament satellite data recorders. After some investigation, you learn they were gathered by a Flufftail Fox Ero once saved called "Fluffball," who tried to repay his kindness in its own way. To keep Ero's tent from becoming a junk heap again, and for the sake of future research, you contact the Spacetrek Collective and turn the recorders over to them.

A glitching order in the cafeteria's food machine leads you to a strange patch of blue snow in the frostlands. A research team, determined to study the frostlands' Cobalt Sediment structure, pushed into a hazardous zone and never returned. Following the clues left in the order records, you find the vehicle they once used, along with a non-standard component and their logs. The logs describe how their obsession with tracing the strange structure slowly drove them mad. I.R.I.S. recovers the component, and you decide it's best to let that cobalt dream remain buried beneath the snow.

Back to Lahai-Roi, Aemeath waits for you on a bench in the Academy. Now "reborn," she is ready to continue her studies there. One day, she hopes to travel farther and save even more people. As the two of you stroll through Lahai-Roi's spring breeze, you promise that no matter what path she chooses, you will always be proud of her.

Hiyuki speaks on behalf of Lucilla to let you know how things will be handled after the Aleph-1 incident. She also fills you in on what's happening in Ashinohara and what the Fractsidus have been up to lately. Their plan against her has failed, and after going through life-and-death situations by your side, she has finally let go of her wish to save Ashinohara all by herself.

At the request of Ham, the director of the Spacetrek Incubation Program, you help four research teams funded by the program push past their setbacks and finish their reports. Ham tells you that while their work may not seem groundbreaking, it's a crucial step forward on the path of scientific discovery. He believes that with the Academy's support, these students will one day rise like new stars and light up the skies above Lahai-Roi.

Zenus, a student whose proposal was rejected by the Spacetrek Incubation Program, still refuses to abandon his project. Determined to deepen humanity's understanding of Solaris, he plans to deploy high-sensitivity seismometers across the Dimmr Plains to map the region. You help him place the instruments at three of the most dangerous sites, while Ham, the very teacher who once turned him down, helps with the deployment of the remaining survey equipment. Once the data is successfully recovered, Zenus gets his drive back with your support and resolves to continue his relentless commitment to research.

Reynard, hoping to take a shortcut on his field assignment, gets tricked by a mysterious group known as the "Retrievers." Not only does he fail to finish the assignment, but he also gets swindled out of a large sum of money. He comes to you for help in finding out who the Retrievers really are. Together, you track down the people they once served. You discover that even when what they recovered was nothing more than a forgery, grieving people still clung to it for comfort. After you shut down the Retrievers' operation, a business built on profiting from people's sorrow, Reynard is deeply moved. He decides to become a true Retriever instead: someone who can recover what's been lost and help ease the pain of those who are grieving.

The Spacetrek Collective finishes sorting through the Fractsidus records recovered in the Dimmr Plains. Arman invites you to meet with him in person and shares what they found. From those materials, you finally learn the truth behind Denia's plan. Later, Sigrika tracks you down and tells you that before she left, Denia wrote her a letter confessing everything. Now that she knows the truth, Sigrika is finally able to accept her friend's decision to leave and face the future with renewed hope.

On the forty-second full moon of my knighthood, a young man stabbed the right of my abdomen. In retaliation, I took his life. The Order rewarded my killings and celebrated my bloodlust. Yet Sentinel, if my words reach you, I beg for clarity: is mercy the path to saving grace or a swift descent into an early grave?

On the first full moon of my knighthood, I was defeated by a band of Plushies. The big Plushie was more terrifying than I imagined—a slight hesitation almost cost me my life. I was lucky to survive. But Sentinel, I ask you to witness how I conquer my fear and become unyielding. Under your divine gaze, I will forge myself into the very embodiment of the Five Knightly Virtues!

On the hundred and forty-fourth full moon of my knighthood, I was ordered to write a book on an island—despite my illiteracy. I wanted to share my techniques for fighting Tacet Discords, but the Acolytes suggested I center my words around the Five Knightly Virtues. O Sentinel, perhaps you can't hear this, but in all my supposed wisdom, I might be the most foolish of all.

On the ninetieth full moon of my knighthood, I was assigned to duel on the great bridge. Day after day, knights came to challenge me, only to fall again and again—all to hasten my so-called glory of a hundred victories. O Sentinel, do you hear me? The weight of honor grows heavier, yet my sword feels ever more brittle.

On the ninety-fifth full moon of my knighthood, I managed to gather fifteen crates of donations. After giving dues to the Order and the family I serve, only five remained. Even with the three crates I donated... No, it's not enough. It's nowhere near enough! O Sentinel, please enlighten me: why do the greediest souls always hide behind the banner of generosity?

Evaluation Basis: Dhalifa's Medical Report

The patient's Tacet Mark is located on the upper right arm. The precise time of Awakening cannot be determined. Upon admission, the patient was conscious but non-communicative. When asked about her Forte, she applied it to a clock in the ward, increasing its accuracy to within femtoseconds.

The patient later clarified, via a caregiver robot, that her Forte can randomly impact machine performance. For instance, a different clock affected by her Forte began running slowly, and became unresponsive to recalibration.

As inquiries were made solely to ensure treatment safety, no further investigation is planned.

"A femtosecond is one quadrillionth of a second. The precision is astonishing. Send this clock to Startorch Academy. They'll know what to do with it."

Conclusion: Resonant Criticality is moderate. Patient stability is also moderate, with minimal risk of Overclocking.
A prior history of Overclocking is documented. 
Maximum severity rating: Moderate.

The patient previously Overclocked during a Void Storm, drawing Exoswarm material to her body to replace contaminated tissue, which enabled her survival. The embedded material now shows no Exoswarm frequency and functions solely as prosthetic tissue.

The patient currently demonstrates unusually stable emotional states considering her trauma and injuries. Regular evaluation and psychological support are recommended.

"Dhalifa survived only by Overclocking. This is not an ability that can counter Void Storms! Make sure the Department of Voidmatters leaves her alone!"

A rust-stained electronic sheep toy, loose and wobbly, as if it could fall apart at any moment.

Dhalifa grew bored with this simple gadget almost immediately. But the instant she discovered that turning a single screw, nudging a bearing, or rerouting a thin line of circuitry could make the toy spin, tumble, or even bleat, something inside her ignited.

From that moment on, she seized every chance to pester the visiting Spacetrek Collective researchers with endless questions. It was also the point when the more conservative members of her tribe began to alienate her for her newfound obsession.

A length of plain, monotone silk, embroidered with the names of the Roya lost to the Void Storm that ravaged the Spacetrek Observatory. Dhalifa's name is there as well, yet a single strand of violet thread crosses it out.

"…In short, developing high-performance combat mechs had become a pressing need.

The project was assigned to a pair of twin researchers: an older sister who was bold and daring, and a younger sister who was quiet and steady. Their personalities shaped the Twin Nova series they created.

The melee model, Twin Nova: Collapsar Blade, engages with fast and aggressive actions, while its ranged counterpart, Twin Nova: Nebulous Cannon, prefers to stay back and provide support. Their very names embody the Spacetrek Collective's mission: to descend into the unknown as they continue to reach for the stars.

The idea of building the mechs in pairs began as something almost poetic. The Threnodian of Void, Aleph-1, erases individuals from memory, and the twins couldn't imagine a world where they might forget each other. They hoped their creations, at least, would always have a companion and never face that silence alone. While Aleph-1's influence may not extend to inorganic matter, this sentiment became the emotional core of the Twin Nova project.

This philosophy also influenced their form. The Collective opted for humanoid frames to symbolize humanity's presence on the frontier. Rumor has it the design also helps them seem less intimidating when serving as security at Startorch Academy, and perhaps caters to a few researchers' personal tastes.

An autonomous tactical intelligence model was built for the units. However, with little combat data available in the Collective, the sisters had to pilot the prototypes themselves to generate the initial data. Their influence made the Twin Nova units move with a graceful, almost showy flair, a style that is sometimes more artistic than practical.

Now, with the accumulating real combat data, the models continue to evolve. The melee unit leads the charge and breaks through enemy lines, while the ranged unit coordinates with human teams, offering support fire and protecting the formation."

"The sprawling, secret-filled lands of Lahai-Roi made it necessary for the Spacetrek Collective to establish mid-to-long-term field research programs. However, sustaining these operations in such dangerous terrain required dependable mobile bases.

After weighing its options, the Collective developed a versatile transport platform capable of handling logistics, storage, and emergency defense. They named it Spacetrek Explorer.

The Explorer's design is based on a wheel robot. Its massive tires provide exceptional grip, allowing it to climb smooth vertical surfaces and easily navigate the dense architecture of Startorch Academy, delivering cargo to otherwise inaccessible locations. The large storage container mounted on its top further supports fieldwork, enabling researchers to access supplies or auxiliary equipment directly on-site.

To defend against the Exoswarm affected by the Waveworn Phenomenon and attacks from Outcasts, the Explorer is equipped with a heavy electromagnetic cannon and a protective shield projector. However, due to its weight, frequent cargo load, and energy-saving design, it carries only small thrusters. These are useful for brief bursts of acceleration, but not for sustained flight.

In addition to field expeditions, the Spacetrek Explorer now serves as one of Lahai-Roi's primary heavy logistics vehicles. In its logistics configuration, its weapons are removed and replaced with expanded storage modules to maximize cargo capacity."

"Operators must follow the steps below with strict attention to operate Route Constructors.

Step 1: Put in the required amount of Compressed Bedrock.
Note: Compressed Bedrock is processed material made of natural minerals. After refining native Lahai-Roi stone, the Spacetrek Collective produces a high-density construction medium. Once parsed and separated by the Route Constructor, it can be combined with other resources to form structural baseplates for various building types.

Step 2: Put in the required amount of Mechanite.
Note: Mechanite is a native Lahai-Roi mineral. After the arrival of the Exostrider, mechanical patterns and structures started to grow on it under the influence. The Collective has found that electronic devices made with this mineral exhibit increased computational performance, as if the Mechanite itself has processing capability.

Step 3: Put in the required amount of Constructor Cores.
Note: Constructor Cores are artificial power units designed for the equipment's operation. Since the Route Constructor's immense energy demands, remote deployment, and single-use nature make stable energy lines impractical, the Collective developed these cores to serve as portable, reusable "batteries." They are charged by focusing the Reactor's light through a Solis Lens Array.

Step 4: Verify the construction blueprint.
Note: Blueprints are usually pre-loaded during setup. Only a simple confirmation is required.

Step 5: Ensure the construction area is fully cleared of any personnel, animals, or Exoswarm units.

Step 6: Activate the Route Constructor."

"The Relay Station combines garage, warehouse, rest areas, and basic laboratory facilities in a single complex, providing support for arduous field research and logistics operations. One of its key services is vehicle rental.

The station primarily offers three types of vehicles:
- Hauler: A large vehicle designed for transporting heavy cargo.
- Pathfinder: A medium-sized vehicle for personnel transfer, with limited cargo capacity.
- Sprinter: A small vehicle optimized for rapid, solo transport.
 
Due to limited vehicle availability, all applicants must submit a formal request. The staff will review each application and assign vehicles based on demonstrated need.

'Lately, it seems like all the Haulers in Lahai-Roi are heading to the Spacetrek Observatory. Just how massive is that project?'"

"The Spacetrek Observatory stands as a monumental achievement co-built by the Spacetrek Collective and the Roya. Its mission is to map Lahai-Roi's various data points. Unlike the Cassettes that store personal data, the Observatory primarily captures and tracks the changes in Lahai-Roi's terrain, ecology, climate, and sky under the influence of Void Storms and Threnodian activity.

As our partnership with the Roya deepened, the Observatory grew to also document their architecture and cultural landmarks. But then, disaster struck. A devastating Void Storm swept through, leaving the structure in ruins. Although the Academy has started the reconstruction, progress has been painstakingly slow. The sheer number of ongoing projects across Lahai-Roi, coupled with the damaged roads leading to the site, has left this massive facility languishing.

That concludes the introduction to the Spacetrek Observatory. I trust you can now appreciate its importance. Despite the current challenges, its restoration is a necessity! That is why I am calling on each and every one of you to join me in this vital endeavor. We need your help, in whatever form you can offer. Every contribution matters.

My name is Rakosan. I will be here, at the Spacetrek Observatory, waiting for you!"

Alienated by their tribes, openly rejecting tradition, or lured by an insatiable curiosity for a world they had never seen, a group of Roya set out on a path separate from their people. They began trading in Exostrider cell remnants and Exoswarm materials to fulfill their own desires.

Their actions were intolerable to the rest of the Roya. As a result, they were exiled and branded Outcasts. But they did not see this as a punishment, but a liberation, a chance to embrace their true natures. They spread across Lahai-Roi, becoming a force of unrestrained chaos. Their defiance was more than a simple rejection of tradition. They actively inverted it, mocking the old ways in every gesture, every object, and every action.

They cast aside ornaments drawn from nature, instead tearing skulls from the Exoswarm to wear as grisly masks. They reforged their Shepherd's Staffs into weapons.

But what exactly is their purpose? Some say they see themselves as the new, true branch of the Roya, striving to carve out a place in a changing world. These, however, are only rumors. In truth, the Outcasts demonstrate no unified ideology and voice no common demands. They appear consumed instead by the thrill of discovery and the hunt for the Exoswarm.
